landingAct1.line2: It has been for a while.
landingAct1.valueProp: VegaDūta - the enterprise agentic AI platform where AI agents run your workflows, not just your chat.

landingAct2.assembled: Underneath every task, there are layers most people never see.
landingAct2.trace: system.reasoning.trace → evaluating 4 candidate approaches, selecting highest-confidence path
landingAct2.hint: Move your cursor over the line above

landingAct3.tagline: Not a chatbot. Not a script. An intelligence that acts.
landingAct3.subtagline: The enterprise platform for building, orchestrating, and scaling AI agents across every business workflow.

landingAct5.copy: It doesn't wait for you to open an app. It's already where your work happens.

landingAct6.statementPrefix: Every agent runs this same loop - research, plan, execute, validate, report -

landingAxon.heroSubtitle: Build AI agents, give them your knowledge and tools, and put them to work across WhatsApp, Telegram, email and eight more channels — with humans in the loop wherever it matters.
landingAxon.capabilitiesSubtitle: Not a chatbot builder. A living system you can watch, steer, and trust.
landingAxon.capAgentsDesc: Persona, model, temperature, knowledge and tools — from a template or from scratch. Test in the Playground before you ship.
landingAxon.capWorkflowsDesc: Node-based automations with triggers, tool calls and branches. Describe a change in words and watch VegaDūta rewire the graph.
landingAxon.capKnowledgeDesc: Drop in PDFs, docs, images, audio, video. Semantic chunking, embeddings and vector search — grounded, cited answers.
landingAxon.capOmnichannelDesc: WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, Messenger, Slack, Discord, X, email and a mobile SDK — one agent, every inbox.
landingAxon.capToolsDesc: A marketplace of built-in tools and external MCP servers. Agents pick what they need — no manual wiring.
landingAxon.capHitlDesc: Approve sensitive actions before they happen. Every decision is logged in an append-only audit trail.
landingAxon.multilingualBody: The whole console is available in 22 Indian languages, kept fresh with LLM-backed translation, and agents reply in the language your customer writes in. Meet customers on WhatsApp in Hindi, Tamil, Bengali — however they write.
landingAxon.closeTitle: Put your AI to work today.
landingAxon.closeSubtitle: Free tier: 5 agents, 3 workflows, every channel. No card required.
landingAxon.footerTagline: the command center for your AI workforce · made in India 🇮🇳

landingExplore.heroSubtitle: Build agents, ground them in your knowledge, and put them to work across WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram and email — with a human hand on every decision that matters.
landingExplore.bentoTitle: Design it. Ground it. Ship it everywhere.
landingExplore.bento_designerDesc: Drag agents, tools and guardrails onto an infinite canvas. Press Run and watch every packet move through the graph.
landingExplore.bento_live40sDesc: Connect your WhatsApp Business number through Meta Cloud API or Twilio and your agents answer there. Telegram, Instagram and email are one click each.
landingExplore.bento_groundedDesc: Drop in docs, sites and sheets. Every answer cites your sources — no hallucinated policies, ever.
landingExplore.bento_humansDesc: Set the lines your agents never cross alone. Refunds, contracts, deletions — held for a person, every time.
landingExplore.step1Desc: Name it, give it a personality, and tell it what it's allowed to do — in plain language.
landingExplore.step2Desc: Upload docs or point it at your site. It answers with your facts and cites its sources.
landingExplore.step3Desc: Connect WhatsApp through Meta Cloud API or Twilio. Your agent answers customers before your coffee cools.
landingExplore.closeTitleLine2: Put an intelligence on the line.
landingExplore.closeNote: free tier · 500 messages / mo · cancel anytime

billing.heroSubtitle: Everything is free for your first 3 months, for everyone who registers, no card required. After that the Free plan takes over automatically - never mid-conversation, never without warning, and never a surprise bill.
billing.freeBothRegionsNote: Free in every region - no card required.

billing.freeModeTitle: Open source. Free while we launch.
billing.freeModeSubtitle: VegaDūta is an open-source agentic AI platform built by a small team. Every feature and every channel is free to explore, experiment and run while we launch - no card needed. To keep the infrastructure and the team going, we will introduce pricing later; we will announce it well ahead. Bring your own keys, run on-device edge models, or experiment on the hosted pool.
billing.freeModeFeature1: Agents, workflows and team seats - all open to you at launch
billing.freeModeFeature2: Your models, your way - BYOK, on-device edge, or hosted pool
billing.freeModeFeature4: WhatsApp, Telegram, Email and every channel
billing.freeModeFeature5: Full edit access - nothing locked during launch

billing.freeModeCoffeeNote: Built and maintained by a small team of developers. If VegaDūta helps you, a coffee keeps it going.

personal-assistant.title: Personal assistant

research-analyst.body: Answers from pages it actually read, cites each one and lists what it could not verify.

meeting-notes-to-actions.title: Meeting notes to actions

connectHub.title: Connect your world
connectHub.subtitle: Choose where your agent talks to you and what it can read. Each card opens the page that does it.
connectHub.intro: Start with one. Telegram is the quickest: it works on any install with nothing but a bot token.
connectHub.privacy: Passwords and keys are stored encrypted and never shown to the model. You can disconnect any of these at any time.

telegram.title: Telegram
telegram.body: Talk to your agent from your phone. Create a bot with BotFather, paste its token, and it answers. No public web address needed.

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp
whatsapp.body: Link your own number by scanning a QR code - your agent answers as you. Works on a laptop install, no public web address needed. (The official Meta API is under Channels for hosted setups.)

email.title: Email
email.body: Give your agent an inbox it can read and reply from. Replies wait for your approval.

google.title: Google: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets
google.body: Let your agent read your calendar, draft replies, find files and fill in spreadsheets. You approve anything it sends.

slack.title: Slack
slack.body: Bring your agent into your team's Slack so people can ask it in a channel or a direct message.

sms.title: Text messages (SMS)
sms.body: Reach your agent from any phone, even without a data plan.

knowledge.title: Your documents
knowledge.body: Upload files and web pages so the agent answers from your own material, with sources.

startFlow.title: Get your first agent running
startFlow.subtitle: Three short steps: choose what you want to do, set it up in one click, then try it. Nothing is sent to a model until you press Send.

startFlow.goalHeading: What do you want to do?
startFlow.goalHint: Pick the closest match. You can go back and choose again at any point.
startFlow.goalLearnBody: Get a tutor that builds short lessons around a topic you choose.
startFlow.goalResearchBody: An assistant that breaks a question into parts and keeps what comes from sources apart from what it already knows.
startFlow.goalAnalyzeBody: An assistant that works out the numbers in your data by running code, and shows the script it used.
startFlow.goalAutomateBody: Describe a task in one sentence and get a draft workflow to review.
startFlow.goalDraftBody: Turn call notes into a summary, action items and a follow-up reply you can edit and send yourself.

explainersWorkflow.waitIntro: A Wait node pauses a run without keeping anything running.
explainersWorkflow.waitReachTitle: The run reaches the Wait node
explainersWorkflow.waitReachBody: The time or date is worked out now, including any expressions. A time that has already passed, or a wait of zero, does not pause at all. Test runs that simulate sends skip the wait.
explainersWorkflow.waitParkedBody: The pause is stored, so it survives restarts. While the run is parked no step runs and no model is called.
explainersWorkflow.waitWakeTimeBody: A scheduled sweep wakes the run at or shortly after the time, usually within about a minute.
explainersWorkflow.waitWakeCallTitle: A call arrives, or the wait gives up
explainersWorkflow.waitOutcomeCallBody: a POST to the run's private resume link continues the run.
explainersWorkflow.waitOutcomeTimeoutFailLabel: Nothing arrives in time: Fail the run
explainersWorkflow.waitOutcomeTimeoutFailBody: the run ends as failed. This is the default.
explainersWorkflow.waitOutcomeTimeoutContinueLabel: Nothing arrives in time: Continue the run
explainersWorkflow.waitOutcomeTimeoutContinueBody: the run carries on down the same path. There is no separate timeout branch.
explainersWorkflow.waitResumeTitle: The run continues at the next node
explainersWorkflow.waitResumeTimeBody: The next node receives exactly what the Wait node received.
explainersWorkflow.waitResumeCallBody: The next node receives the posted JSON as "resume" next to the original "input". After a timeout that continues, it receives "timedOut": true instead of "resume".
explainersWorkflow.errorIntro: What happens when this node fails. These settings only take effect when this deployment has the node error strategy switched on.
explainersWorkflow.errorFailsBody: It throws an error or reports a failure.
explainersWorkflow.errorRetryTitle: If retry is on, it is tried again first
explainersWorkflow.errorRetryBody: Up to the total attempts you set, pausing between attempts. A node that can send or change something outside the workflow is not retried unless you allow it.
explainersWorkflow.errorDecideTitle: Still failing: "When this node fails" decides
explainersWorkflow.errorOutcomeStopBody: the run ends as failed. If the red error port is connected, the failure goes there instead.
explainersWorkflow.errorOutcomeContinueLabel: Continue, passing the error on as this node's output
explainersWorkflow.errorOutcomeContinueBody: the run follows the node's normal path, and the next node receives the error message and this node's id. A plan limit or a validation problem still stops the run.
explainersWorkflow.errorOutcomeBranchLabel: Follow the red error port if one is connected, otherwise stop
explainersWorkflow.errorOutcomeBranchBody: the run goes to whatever the red port is wired to. With nothing wired, the run ends as failed.
explainersWorkflow.switchArriveBody: Each case reads its fields from the incoming data.
explainersWorkflow.switchTestTitle: Cases are tested from top to bottom
explainersWorkflow.switchTestBody: A case with no name or no conditions is skipped.
explainersWorkflow.switchOutcomeMatchBody: the run leaves through the port named after that case. Later cases are not checked, even if they would match too.
explainersWorkflow.switchOutcomeDefaultBody: the run leaves through the Default port.
explainersWorkflow.switchPassBody: The next node receives exactly what the Switch received.

agentLab.title: Agent Lab
agentLab.launcherTooltip: Open Agent Lab: run graph, prompt knockout and consistency check
agentLab.subtitle: testing {name}
agentLab.noAgent: Select an agent to use the lab.
agentLab.capabilitiesLoading: Checking what this workspace can run…
agentLab.capabilitiesUnsupported: This instrument needs a newer server version and is not available here yet.
agentLab.planLockedReason: Prompt knockout and consistency checks make many model calls and are a Premium feature.
agentLab.scopeNote: Lab runs ask the model directly, using this agent's prompt, sampling settings and the model it normally answers with. They do not use tools, memory, knowledge lookups, guardrails, response caching, cost routing, learned model routing or fallback providers, and they are not added to the conversation.
agentLab.estimateOverCap: That is over the limit of {cap} model calls per run. Reduce the selection.
agentLab.estimateUsageNote: Calls count toward your usual usage limits. A run stops after 20 minutes and keeps the results so far.
agentLab.statusCancelled: Cancelled. Results so far are shown.
agentLab.statusExpired: This run is no longer available. Results are kept for {minutes} minutes.
agentLab.statusLost: Lost contact with the server. The run may still be going.
agentLab.partialResults: Partial results: the run did not finish.
agentLab.graphEmpty: Send a message in the playground to see its run graph here.
agentLab.graphNoSteps: This turn reported no intermediate steps. The model answered directly.
agentLab.graphNoReply: This message has no reply. The send failed or was cancelled before the agent answered.
agentLab.graphCanvasLabel: Run graph for the selected turn
agentLab.graphInspectHint: Select a step in the graph to inspect it.
agentLab.graphPreviewNote: Arguments and results are shortened previews of up to 400 characters and may be redacted.
agentLab.graphForkBody: The conversation is rewound to just before this message, and the message is sent again. Later turns are removed from the live conversation, and the server's running summary of older turns is rebuilt as the conversation continues. The current version is kept as a read-only snapshot so you can compare the two.
agentLab.graphForkSideEffects: Tool calls the original turn already made are not undone.
agentLab.graphForkAttachmentNote: Attachments from the original message are not sent again.
agentLab.graphForkCacheNote: This agent has response caching turned on. Sending the same message again can return the stored original answer without calling the model, so the branch may be a copy of the original. Edit the message to get a fresh answer. With semantic caching, a lightly edited message can still return a stored answer.
agentLab.graphForkEstimate: This runs 1 agent turn. A turn can make several model calls depending on reasoning depth and tools.
agentLab.graphForkBusy: Wait for the current turn to finish before forking.
agentLab.graphForkNoSession: There is no server session to rewind yet.
agentLab.graphForkOnDevice: This turn was answered on this device and never reached the server session, so it cannot be rewound.
agentLab.graphForkTailUnclean: This turn or a later one cannot be rewound because it ran on this device, was refused, was answered from cache, was interrupted, failed or is still running. Forking here is not available.
agentLab.graphForkPrefixUnclean: An earlier turn in this conversation failed, was refused, was interrupted or was answered from cache, so the server's stored messages cannot be matched to this transcript. Clear context and try again in a fresh conversation.
agentLab.graphForkMismatch: The server session holds {server} stored messages but this transcript accounts for {local}. Voice calls, a tool approval, a very long conversation or an expired session can cause this. Clear context and try again in a fresh conversation.
agentLab.graphForkSnapshotNotStored: This browser refused to store the snapshot (its storage is full or blocked), so the original would be kept only until this page is reloaded or closed. Nothing has been rewound. Press Rewind and re-run again to go ahead anyway.
agentLab.graphForkUnknown: The rewind request failed and the server session could not be confirmed unchanged: {reason} The conversation may have been rewound. The snapshot of the original is kept under Compare. Clear context before continuing this conversation.
agentLab.graphForkInterleaved: The conversation was rewound, but another turn started before the message could be sent again, so it was not re-sent. The playground transcript no longer matches the server session. The original is kept under Compare. Clear context before continuing this conversation.
agentLab.graphForkResendFailed: The conversation was rewound, but the re-sent message got no reply. Close the lab to see the error in the playground. The original is kept under Compare.
agentLab.graphCompareNone: No snapshots yet. Fork a turn to keep its original for comparison.
agentLab.graphCompareDetached: The live conversation has moved on from this fork, so only the original is shown.
agentLab.graphCompareRemovedTurns: {count} later turns of the original were removed from the live conversation.
agentLab.graphCompareRemovedTurnsOne: 1 later turn of the original was removed from the live conversation.
agentLab.graphCompareSameTools: Both versions called the same tools.
agentLab.graphSnapshotNote: Snapshots are kept in this browser only, for 24 hours.
agentLab.koIntro: Remove one section of the system prompt at a time and measure how the score changes on the same questions.
agentLab.koNoPrompt: This agent has no system prompt to split.
agentLab.koPromptTooLong: This prompt is longer than {max} characters, which is more than a lab run can send.
agentLab.koSectionsHint: The prompt is split at headings and blank lines. Untick a section to leave it out of the test.
agentLab.koSectionsMerged: The prompt has more than {max} parts, so the smallest neighbours were merged.
agentLab.koDatasetNone: No eval datasets for this agent yet. Use probe questions, or create a dataset on the Quality page.
agentLab.koDatasetNote: Cases with an expected answer are scored against it.
agentLab.koProbesPlaceholder: How do I reset my password?
agentLab.koProbesNote: Probe questions have no reference answer, so the judge scores how well each answer addresses the question.
agentLab.koItemsTrimmed: Only the first {max} questions are used.
agentLab.koItemTooLong: Question {n} is longer than {max} characters. Shorten it or leave it out.
agentLab.koTooFewToLabel: This is too little to tell a real change from noise, so no section could be labelled. Use at least {items} questions, and enough baseline repeats that questions × (repeats − 1) is {df} or more. Add a question or a baseline repeat.
agentLab.koRepeatsHint: The unchanged prompt is run this many times to measure the noise floor.
agentLab.koMeasuredOn: Measured on {items} questions, baseline repeated {repeats} times.
agentLab.koMeasuredOnOne: Measured on 1 question, baseline repeated {repeats} times.
agentLab.koNoiseFloorHelp: Estimated from how much the score varied between identical baseline runs, widened for the number of sections tested. A smaller change cannot be told apart from run-to-run variation.
agentLab.koNoBaseline: Not enough baseline scores to estimate the noise floor, so no section can be labelled.
agentLab.koLiveNote: The run is still going. The changes measured so far are shown. Labels and the noise floor appear when it finishes.
agentLab.koDeltaHelp: Bars show the score lost when the section is removed: a bar to the right means the section helps. The per-question table shows the change itself, the score without the section minus the baseline.
agentLab.koDetailLoadBearing: Removing it lowered the score by {delta}.
agentLab.koDetailHarmful: Removing it raised the score by {delta}.
agentLab.koDetailNoEffect: A change of {delta} is inside the noise floor.
agentLab.koDetailNotMeasured: No question produced a usable score for this section.
agentLab.koDetailNoFloor: Removing it changed the score by {change}, but there is too little data to tell that apart from noise, so it is not labelled.
agentLab.koDetailPending: Removing it has changed the score by {change} so far.
agentLab.koDetailPendingNone: No score for this section yet.
agentLab.koItemsAgree: {agree} of {total} questions moved the same way.
agentLab.koCaveat: Scores come from an LLM judge running on the same model as the agent. Small samples give rough estimates, so treat a label as a lead to check, not a verdict.
agentLab.koChartLabel: Score lost when the section is removed, with the noise floor shaded
agentLab.ccIntro: Ask the same question several times and see whether the answers mean the same thing.
agentLab.ccNoTurns: No server turns in the playground yet. Type a question instead.
agentLab.ccIncludeHistory: Include the conversation before this turn ({count} messages)
agentLab.ccToolsWarning: The original turn used tools. Samples are generated without tools, so they may differ from it for that reason.
agentLab.wtHelp: Off: each answer is one plain model call. On: answers come from the same tool pipeline a chat turn uses, so tools run, guardrails apply and step limits hold. A call that needs a person's approval waits as a pending approval.
agentLab.wtUnavailable: Running the lab with tools is turned off on this install. Ask an administrator to enable it.
agentLab.wtActive: Tools will run for real in this run, including any side effects.
agentLab.wtConfirmTitle: Run the lab with the agent's tools?
agentLab.wtConfirmBody: Every sample can call the agent's real tools, and those calls can have real effects such as sending a message or writing data. Calls that need approval will wait for a person. Use this only with a test agent or test data.
agentLab.ccZeroTempNote: This agent's temperature is 0, so samples will usually match.
agentLab.ccDetailMixed: Answers disagree: {majority} of {n} agree and the rest differ.
agentLab.ccDetailUnstable: Answers disagree: no answer has a majority across {n} samples.
agentLab.ccDetailInsufficient: Only {n} of {k} samples finished, which is too few to compare.
agentLab.ccDetailUnverified: Comparisons without a verdict: {count}. The answers could not be grouped reliably, so run the check again.
agentLab.ccDetailContradictory: Every answer matched the first one, but the judge also called some of them different from each other (pairs: {count}). The verdicts contradict each other, so run the check again.
agentLab.ccUnknownNote: Comparisons without a verdict: {count}. Counting them as same or as different gives the same result.

nodeDefs.triggerDescription: Starts a run - inbound message, schedule, or manual.
nodeDefs.agentDescription: Runs a configured agent against the current input.
nodeDefs.knowledgeDescription: Retrieves context from a knowledge collection.
nodeDefs.conditionDescription: Branches true/false on whether input contains a phrase.
nodeDefs.approvalDescription: Pauses the run for a human sign-off via the Approvals inbox.
nodeDefs.outputDescription: Sends the result out - log it, or publish a workflow event.
nodeDefs.device_controlDescription: Queues a command (tap, type, open app) for a paired phone - fire-and-forget, see the run log.
nodeDefs.toolDescription: Calls one specific tool from a chosen agent's toolkit directly - no LLM turn needed.
nodeDefs.loopDescription: Repeats the very next node once per item in a list, collecting every result into an array.
nodeDefs.codeDescription: Applies a built-in transform (extract a field, regex replace, template, case, JSON parse/stringify) - not arbitrary code.
nodeDefs.workflowDescription: Runs a different, already-saved workflow synchronously and uses its result as this node's output.
nodeDefs.supervisorDescription: An agent picks one of several named routes based on the input - like Condition, but the decision is made by the model.
nodeDefs.parallelDescription: Runs every connected branch at the same time against the same input, then merges the results.
nodeDefs.fan_outDescription: Runs the very next node once per item in a list, all at the same time - like Loop, but concurrent - merging the results into an array.
nodeDefs.human_inputDescription: Pauses the run to collect structured data (a form) from a person, then resumes with the answers.
nodeDefs.sub_flowDescription: Runs a whole embedded sub-graph once per item in a list - multi-step iteration, merging results into an array.
nodeDefs.crm_leadDescription: Creates or updates a lead in the Leads CRM, moves it to a pipeline stage, or adds an activity to its timeline.
nodeDefs.voice_menuDescription: A phone-call menu: speaks a prompt, collects keypad (DTMF) digits with a timeout and retries, then branches on what the caller pressed.
nodeDefs.bulk_emailDescription: Sends a personalized email to many recipients - throttled, with an unsubscribe link, a suppression list and reply detection.
nodeDefs.data_tableDescription: Reads or writes rows in a data table - the workspace's built-in spreadsheet store - so a workflow can keep state between runs.

agentTemplates.dealerOrderDeskKnowledgeHint: Upload the current price list, scheme circulars and credit-terms policy - it always names the slab or scheme it quoted.
agentTemplates.distributorSchemeAssistantTagline: Explains current trade schemes, slabs and return policy to retailers, with the circular and validity date.
agentTemplates.distributorSchemeAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload scheme circulars with their validity periods, plus the credit and return policy. Stale circulars produce stale answers, so keep them current.
agentTemplates.farmerAdvisoryAssistantTagline: Answers farmers in their own language from your agronomy advisories - never a dosage or diagnosis it invented.
agentTemplates.farmerAdvisoryAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload your package-of-practices, advisories, product labels and dosage charts. This agent quotes them verbatim and refuses to answer beyond them.
agentTemplates.agriInputDealerAssistantTagline: Handles seed, fertiliser and crop-protection counter enquiries and order requests from your catalogue and labels.
agentTemplates.agriInputDealerAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the product catalogue and approved product labels - label dosage is repeated verbatim, never paraphrased.
agentTemplates.insurancePolicyAssistantTagline: Explains cover, exclusions, waiting periods and renewals from your policy wordings, pointing to the clause.
agentTemplates.insurancePolicyAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload policy wordings, brochures, prospectuses and servicing FAQs. It cannot see a customer's policy record, so everything specific goes to your team.
agentTemplates.insuranceClaimIntakeAssistantTagline: Takes first-notice-of-loss details and the document checklist, and hands a tidy summary to your claims team.
agentTemplates.insuranceClaimIntakeAssistantKnowledgeHi: Upload the claims process documents, intimation timelines and document checklists. It records a claim; it never decides one.
agentTemplates.loanProductExplainerTagline: Explains eligibility, documents and published rate ranges for an NBFC, branch or DSA - never a sanction.
agentTemplates.loanProductExplainerKnowledgeHint: Upload product sheets, rate cards and eligibility criteria. It never asks for an account number, card number, OTP or PIN, and warns customers who offer one.
agentTemplates.caClientDocumentCollectorTagline: Chases exactly the documents a filing or audit still needs, from your firm's own engagement checklists.
agentTemplates.caClientDocumentCollectorKnowledgeHint: Upload the firm's engagement checklists and due-date calendar. Tax positions and notices stay with the partner - it collects, it does not advise.
agentTemplates.schoolOfficeAssistantTagline: Answers parents on admissions, fees, timings and circulars in their own language, and logs enquiries.
agentTemplates.schoolOfficeAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the prospectus, fee structure, admission notices, academic calendar and transport routes. It never discusses an individual student.
agentTemplates.corporateTrainingTutorTagline: Tutors learners strictly inside your curriculum, so every answer matches what they will be assessed on.
agentTemplates.corporateTrainingTutorKnowledgeHint: Upload the curriculum, slide decks, handbooks and assessments. Anything outside them it declines rather than answering from general knowledge.
agentTemplates.projectSalesEnquiryAssistantTagline: Answers buyers on floor plans, payment schedule, RERA details and possession - only from approved documents.
agentTemplates.projectSalesEnquiryAssistantKnowledgeHin: Upload the RERA registration, approved floor plans and carpet areas, price list, payment schedule and specifications.
agentTemplates.vendorBoqAssistantTagline: Reads tender documents and BOQs and lays vendor quotations side by side on the lines they share.
agentTemplates.vendorBoqAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the tender documents, BOQ, specifications and the vendor quotations you are comparing. It flags omissions rather than filling them.
agentTemplates.eventEnquiryQuotationAssistantTagline: Answers package and menu questions and turns an enquiry into an itemised draft quotation for you to send.
agentTemplates.eventEnquiryQuotationAssistantKnowledgeH: Upload menus, package sheets, venue capacities, the rate card and the advance/cancellation policy.
agentTemplates.vehicleShowroomAssistantTagline: Compares variants, explains on-road breakup and finance illustrations, and captures test-drive requests.
agentTemplates.vehicleShowroomAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload brochures, variant and price lists, accessory lists and the published finance illustration sheet.
agentTemplates.tourPackageAssistantTagline: Walks travellers through itineraries, inclusions, exclusions and visa checklists from your own tariff sheets.
agentTemplates.tourPackageAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload package itineraries, inclusions and exclusions, tariff sheets, visa document checklists and the cancellation policy.
agentTemplates.hotelPreStayAssistantTagline: Handles the questions guests actually ask before and during a stay, and routes in-stay requests to the desk.
agentTemplates.hotelPreStayAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload room types, the tariff sheet, amenities, F&B timings, house rules and local-area notes.
agentTemplates.salonBookingAssistantTagline: Shares services, prices and stylist availability and captures appointment requests for the desk to confirm.
agentTemplates.salonBookingAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the service menu with prices and durations, stylist or therapist specialisations, and product/aftercare notes.
agentTemplates.fitnessMembershipAssistantTagline: Explains plans, classes and freeze rules, and captures trial and sign-up interest - never a training plan.
agentTemplates.fitnessMembershipAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload membership plans, the class schedule, trainer profiles, facility rules and the freeze/cancellation policy.
agentTemplates.textileBuyerEnquiryAssistantTagline: Answers buyers on composition, GSM, shades, MOQ and lead time, and logs swatch and sample requests.
agentTemplates.textileBuyerEnquiryAssistantKnowledgeHin: Upload the product catalogue, fabric specification sheets, shade cards and trade terms. Specifications are repeated exactly, never paraphrased.
agentTemplates.jewelleryShowroomAssistantTagline: Explains purity, hallmarking, making charges and buy-back terms, and captures appointment requests.
agentTemplates.jewelleryShowroomAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the collection catalogue, making-charge structure, hallmarking policy, exchange/buy-back terms and care instructions. It never quotes a rate.
agentTemplates.ngoGrantReportWriterTagline: Drafts funder reports to their own structure, with every number traced to a document you uploaded.
agentTemplates.ngoGrantReportWriterKnowledgeHint: Upload programme documents, monitoring data, past reports and the funder's guidelines. Missing figures become marked placeholders, never estimates.
agentTemplates.citizenSchemeGuideTagline: Explains scheme eligibility, documents and where to apply, in the citizen's own language, from the notification.
agentTemplates.citizenSchemeGuideKnowledgeHint: Upload the official scheme guidelines, notifications and forms. It names the notification and its date so nobody acts on a superseded rule.
agentTemplates.engagementScopingAssistantTagline: Turns a client conversation into a scoped SOW draft - objectives, deliverables and a hard out-of-scope list.
agentTemplates.engagementScopingAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload past statements of work, the rate card, standard terms and your methodology documents.
agentTemplates.diagnosticsLabAssistantTagline: Gives test preparation instructions and captures home-collection requests - and never reads a report.
agentTemplates.diagnosticsLabAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the test menu, preparation instructions, sample requirements, price list and home-collection policy.
agentTemplates.pharmacyCounterAssistantTagline: Handles timings, delivery, stock listings and refill requests - never a dose, substitute or side effect.
agentTemplates.pharmacyCounterAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the catalogue with pack sizes and MRP, delivery areas and charges, and the prescription policy.
agentTemplates.rentalTenantSupportAssistantTagline: Answers tenants and owners from the agreement itself and routes maintenance complaints by your escalation matrix.
agentTemplates.rentalTenantSupportAssistantKnowledgeHin: Upload tenancy agreements, house rules, society bye-laws, maintenance SOPs and the escalation matrix.
agentTemplates.legalMatterStatusAssistantTagline: Drafts a plain-language client status update from the matter file - for an attorney to review and send.
agentTemplates.legalMatterStatusAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload matter notes, cause lists, filing records and your standard update templates. It states nothing the file does not record.
agentTemplates.freightQuotationAssistantTagline: Explains lane rates, chargeable weight and surcharges, and drafts a quotation summary for your desk.
agentTemplates.freightQuotationAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the rate card with its version, lane list, service-area map, surcharge schedule and terms.
agentTemplates.productListingCopyWriterTagline: Writes marketplace titles, bullets and attributes from the spec sheet - marking anything it cannot evidence.
agentTemplates.productListingCopyWriterKnowledgeHint: Upload spec sheets, labels and existing catalogue entries. A missing attribute is written as MISSING, never invented.
agentTemplates.retailOffersFaqAssistantTagline: Answers shoppers on live offers, loyalty, exchange and refund policy with the validity window attached.
agentTemplates.retailOffersFaqAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload offer circulars with validity windows, the loyalty programme terms, and the exchange/refund policy.

agentTemplates.setupStepKnowledgeBody: This template answers from your files, not from general knowledge - with an empty collection it is worse than a plain chat. Create a collection and upload the documents listed above. The Free plan includes one collection.
agentTemplates.setupStepChannelTitle: 2. Put it where your customers are
agentTemplates.setupStepChannelBody: A customer-facing agent that only lives in this console has not really shipped. Connect WhatsApp, Telegram or email on the Channels page and point the channel at this agent.
agentTemplates.setupStepProviderBody: Model, code-execution and voice keys live on the Providers page. Store a key once there and refer to it from the agent; never paste a key into a chat.
agentTemplates.setupStepMcpBody: Open the Tools page and connect the servers listed above. Some activate in one click; the rest need a key or a sign-in first. Only a workspace admin can do this.
agentTemplates.setupStepToolAccessBody: Open the agent's Tools tab and tick the new tools. If the agent has a specific allowed-tools list, a newly connected server stays invisible to it until you add the tools there.

agentsGuide.title: How agents work
agentsGuide.subtitle: An agent is an AI assistant you shape in six quick steps. Here's the whole flow.
agentsGuide.step1Body: Write a system prompt that tells the agent who it is, its tone, and what it should (and shouldn't) do.
agentsGuide.step2Body: Choose the AI model that powers it. Stay on Simple for smart defaults, or switch to Manual to tune temperature, tokens, fallback and cost routing.
agentsGuide.step3Body: Attach knowledge collections so the agent answers from your own documents — with citations — instead of guessing.
agentsGuide.step4Body: Turn on tools and MCP connectors so the agent can take real actions: look things up, call services, and complete tasks end to end.
agentsGuide.step5Body: Chat with the agent live on the right to see exactly how it responds — and which tools it used — before anyone else does.
agentsGuide.step6Body: Happy with it? Deploy the agent to WhatsApp, the web widget, or any other channel and it goes live for your customers.
agentsGuide.footerHint: Reopen this any time from “How it works”.

agentTrifecta.title: Risky tool mix: this agent could leak private data
agentTrifecta.body: It can read private data, take in content written by outsiders, and send data out. Instructions hidden in that outside content could make it send the private data away.
agentTrifecta.advice: Remove one of the three, or make a person approve what it sends.
agentTrifecta.requireApproval: Require approval for every tool call
agentTrifecta.approvalAlreadyOn: Approval is already required for every tool call.

agentTrifecta.enforcedNote: Your workspace requires approval for agents with this tool mix, so this agent now waits for a person before every action.

agentHooks.title: Hooks
agentHooks.subtitle: Rules that run at set points in every run: block or limit a tool, ask a person first, redact sensitive text, add a note, or check with a webhook. Hooks can only make an agent stricter, never looser.
agentHooks.off: Hooks are switched off on this deployment. You can read them here, but they are not enforced and cannot be saved.
agentHooks.noPermission: Changing hooks needs the guardrails permission.
agentHooks.inheritedNote: These apply to every agent and run before this agent's own hooks. They are managed for the whole workspace.
agentHooks.tooMany: An agent can have at most {max} hooks.
agentHooks.webhookHostsNone: No webhook hosts are allowed yet. An admin adds them in the workspace hook defaults.
agentHooks.fieldIncludeData: Send the content too (credential-like fields are always removed)
agentHooks.fieldRegex: Your own patterns (one regular expression per line)
agentHooks.fieldMessage: Message when the limit is hit
agentHooks.afterModelNote: Redacting, blocking or checking the reply holds it back until it is complete, so it will not stream word by word. The change applies to what is delivered: the saved conversation history keeps the original reply.
agentHooks.webhookNote: A webhook can only answer allow or deny. An allow never skips an approval the platform would ask for. Limits and webhooks on a tool call are checked after any human approval, so a call a person approved can still be stopped by them.

block.AFTER_MODEL: replace the reply with a refusal

do.requireApproval: ask a person to approve it first

redact.AFTER_MODEL: redact {kinds} from the delivered reply (the saved conversation keeps the original)

do.limitModel: allow at most {perMinute} model calls per minute
do.limitBoth: allow at most {perRun} calls per run and {perMinute} per minute
do.limitRun: allow at most {perRun} calls per run
do.limitMinute: allow at most {perMinute} calls per minute

appendContext.AFTER_TOOL: append this note to the result: "{note}"

do.webhook: ask {host} to allow or deny (fails {mode} after {timeout} ms)
do.log: record it in the audit trail
do.logLabel: record it in the audit trail as "{label}"

error.idFormat: Use 1 to 40 characters: a-z, 0-9, - and _, starting with a letter or digit.
error.idDuplicate: Another hook already has this name.
error.actionNotAllowed: That action cannot be used at this point.
error.toolGlobFormat: Use letters, digits and _ . : - with * and ? as wildcards (up to 128 characters).
error.limitNeedsNumber: Set a per-run limit, a per-minute limit, or both.
error.limitRange: Use whole numbers: 1 to 1000 per run, 1 to 10000 per minute.
error.patternsRequired: Pick at least one built-in pattern or write your own.
error.regexTooMany: Use at most 5 patterns of your own.
error.regexTooLong: A pattern can be at most 200 characters.
error.regexInvalid: One of your patterns is not a valid regular expression.
error.regexEmpty: A pattern must not match empty text.
error.urlHttps: Use an https URL, for example https://hooks.example.com/check.
error.timeoutRange: Use a whole number from 100 to 5000.

agentWorkbench.reasoningDepthPLANNEDCost: Writes a plan before acting: more model calls per task, and the reply appears all at once instead of streaming.
agentWorkbench.reasoningDepthCAREFULCost: Checks its answer before showing it: slower, and the reply appears all at once instead of streaming.
agentWorkbench.reasoningDepthRIGOROUSCost: Checks its answer before showing it: slower, and the reply appears all at once instead of streaming. Uses the most tokens.

If the triggered run fails or pauses for approval, this node is marked skipped (with the reason in its log) - the parent run keeps going rather than halting automatically. Triggering a chain back on itself is blocked (this workflow is excluded from the list above, and an indirect cycle through other workflows is refused at run time), with a hard 5-level depth cap either way.

memoryPage.title: Memory
memoryPage.subtitle: What your assistants remember about you. Everything here is yours to read, edit and delete.
memoryPage.tab_notes_purpose: Tell assistants who you are and what you are working on, so you never repeat yourself.
memoryPage.tab_assistants_purpose: Choose which assistants may read your notes. Notes do nothing until at least one is switched on.
memoryPage.tab_facts_purpose: What your assistants saved while talking to you. Fix what is wrong, delete what you do not want kept.
memoryPage.tab_import_purpose: Bring in what other assistants know about you, and keep your old chats as read-only records.
memoryPage.tab_privacy_purpose: Download a copy of everything stored about you, or erase all of it.
memoryPage.notesUnusedTitle: No assistant is reading your notes yet
memoryPage.notesUnusedBody: Your notes are only added to chats with assistants that have shared memory turned on, and none do right now.
memoryPage.blocksIntro: Short notes added to conversations with agents that have shared memory turned on, so you do not have to repeat yourself. Empty notes are left out.
memoryPage.personaHint: How you want assistants to talk to you: tone, length, format.
memoryPage.profileHint: Your role, field, tools and anything that shapes good answers.
memoryPage.projectNotesHint: What you are working on right now, in a few lines.
memoryPage.projectsIntro: Keep a note per client or project. A note is only used when your message mentions that project's name.
memoryPage.projectNameInvalid: Use letters, numbers and hyphens, 3 to 40 characters.
memoryPage.projectExists: You already have notes for that project.
memoryPage.factsIntro: Facts saved during conversations. Edit anything that is wrong or delete what you do not want kept.
memoryPage.factsEmptyHint: When you ask an assistant to remember something, it appears here.
memoryPage.deleteConfirm: Delete this memory? This cannot be undone.
memoryPage.loadFailedBody: The request failed, so nothing is shown. Nothing was deleted.

memoryPage.activeProjectHint: Included in every chat until you switch projects.
memoryPage.agentsIntro: Notes are only added to chats with assistants that have shared memory turned on. Turn it on for each assistant that should read them. This is a setting on the assistant, so it applies to everyone who uses that assistant.

memoryPage.agentsNoneBody: You have written notes, but shared memory is off for every assistant, so the notes are not used. Turn it on for at least one assistant below.

memoryPage.dangerIntro: Download a copy of everything stored about you, or erase all of it.
memoryPage.exportHint: A JSON file with every note and every saved memory.

memoryPage.forgetAllDialogBody: All notes, project notes and saved memories will be permanently deleted for every assistant. This cannot be undone. Download a copy first if you may want it later.

memoryPage.forgetAllGraphWarning: The linked-facts index could not be cleared this time, so a few connections may still be recalled. Try again later or contact support.
memoryPage.importIntro: Bring over what ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini remembers about you. You review every line first, and nothing is saved until you press Import.

memoryPage.importRoomFull: There is no room left here, so none of the selected memories can be saved. Delete some memories or choose another place.

chatPortability.importHeading: Import chats from ChatGPT or Claude
chatPortability.importIntro: Bring your conversation history with you. Imported chats are kept as read-only records that only you can see. Nothing is sent to a model, and nothing is added to memory unless you choose it.
chatPortability.step1Title: 1. Export your data from the other app
chatPortability.step1Chatgpt: ChatGPT: Settings, Data controls, Export data. You get an email with a .zip file.
chatPortability.step1Claude: Claude: Settings, Privacy, Export data. You get an email with a .zip file.
chatPortability.step2Body: Choose the .zip you downloaded, or the conversations.json inside it. Attachments are not imported, only their names.
chatPortability.errTooLarge: That file is larger than {size}. Upload just conversations.json from the export.
chatPortability.statsLine: {listed} conversations found, {skipped} could not be used.
chatPortability.scanCapNote: The file holds more conversations than can be read at once. Only the first {count} are listed.
chatPortability.showingFirst: Showing the first {shown} of {total} conversations. Import these, then upload the file again for the rest.
chatPortability.capNote: You can import up to {max} chats at a time.
chatPortability.roomWarning: You have room for {room} more imported chats.
chatPortability.memTitle: Optional: suggest memories from these chats
chatPortability.memBody: Looks for statements you made about yourself, such as where you live or what you use. Nothing is saved until you tick lines and confirm, and each line is screened for secrets first.
chatPortability.memNone: Nothing that looks like a personal fact was found.
chatPortability.memUnavailable: Memory import is not available in this workspace.
chatPortability.memSaved: {saved} memories saved to your shared memory.

chatPortability.viewShortened: Long messages in this chat were shortened on import.
chatPortability.exportNote: Attachments are listed by name only. Chat sessions expire after a while, so export what you want to keep.

researchPage.title: Research
researchPage.subtitle: Ask a question and get a report built from several web sources, with the exact passages quoted and linked so you can check them yourself.
researchPage.runSubtitle: Progress while it works, then the report and its sources.
researchPage.statusFailedTitle: Could not check whether research is available
researchPage.statusFailedBody: The request failed, so nothing is shown. Your earlier runs are not affected.
researchPage.unavailableBody: Research runs are not switched on for this deployment.
researchPage.offTitle: Research is switched off for now
researchPage.offBody: New research cannot be started on this deployment at the moment. Reports from earlier runs stay readable below.

researchPage.needsKeyBody: Web search has not been set up for this deployment yet, so research cannot run. Ask your platform admin to add the search key.

researchPage.runNotFound: This research run was not found. It may belong to another account, or research runs are not available here.
researchPage.parkedBody: This run paused for an approval and will continue once it is approved.
researchPage.progressWorking: Researching. This usually takes a few minutes.
researchPage.progressLeaveNote: You can leave this page. The run keeps going and the report will be here when you come back.
researchPage.failedSchema: The research finished but the report could not be put into its final form. Any text it produced is shown below. Starting the run again usually works.
researchPage.failedGeneric: Something went wrong while researching. Please start the run again.
researchPage.cancelledNote: This run was cancelled before it finished.
researchPage.emptyResult: The run finished without producing a report.
researchPage.traceEmpty: No trace was recorded for this run.
researchPage.plainResultNote: This run did not return a structured report, so its text is shown as written. Source markers in it are not linked.
researchPage.partialNote: Some sources could not be read or a limit was reached, so this report covers only part of the question.
researchPage.unansweredNote: Parts of the question the sources did not settle.
researchPage.noSourcesWarnTitle: This run did not research anything
researchPage.noSourcesWarnBody: No web pages were found or cited, so the text below is the model's own unchecked answer, not a researched report. This usually means the research model ignored its search tool. Run it again, or give the Deep Research agent a stronger model that supports tool use.
researchPage.lexicalNote: The citation check compares wording only. It confirms that a quote appears in the source, not that the source is right.
researchPage.historyLoadFailed: Could not load your research runs.
researchPage.historyEmptyHint: Ask a question above and the run will appear here. Only you can see your runs.
researchPage.historyPageEmptyHint: There are no older runs. Go back to the newer ones.
researchPage.exportCopyFailed: Could not copy. Use the Markdown download instead.
researchPage.exportFailed: The file could not be created. Try again, or use Markdown.
researchPage.exportTimeout: The file is taking longer than expected. It will appear under Files when it is ready, or use Markdown now.

researchPage.entryTitle: Need sources, not just an answer?
researchPage.entryBody: Research reads several web pages for you and writes a report with the exact passages quoted and linked.
researchPage.failedTimeout: The research ran out of time before it finished. Start the run again, or ask a narrower question.

channelsPanel.signalGroupModeAll: Every message in an approved group

channelsPanel.whatsappQrSetupHint: Links your own WhatsApp as a companion device - no Meta Business account needed. Works on a personal install because the bridge dials out to WhatsApp; there is no public webhook.
channelsPanel.whatsappQrNoBridgeHint: This deployment has no WhatsApp QR bridge configured. The operator runs services/whatsapp-qr and sets APP_WHATSAPPQR_BRIDGE_URL and APP_WHATSAPPQR_BRIDGE_SECRET.
channelsPanel.whatsappQrScanHint: In WhatsApp: Settings > Linked devices > Link a device, then point your phone at this code. It refreshes on its own - a new code appears here when it does.

channelsPanel.waQualityHelp: As reported by Meta. Low quality can limit how many people you can message.
channelsPanel.smsRoutingHelp: Anyone can text this Twilio number from any phone, no app or data plan needed. New senders wait for your approval in Pairing; approved senders chat with the agent chosen here. Replies are plain text and cut to fit an SMS. Set the number's "A message comes in" webhook to /webhook/twilio/sms.

channelsPanel.mobileSdkSubtitle: Pair an Android or iOS device
channelsPanel.mobileSdkDownloadHint: Debug build for sideloading only — not on the Play Store yet. Sign-in and device pairing work; the other screens are early previews. Android blocks installs from outside the Play Store by default, so after downloading, open the file and allow "install from this source" when prompted.
channelsPanel.inboundRoutingMissingHint: No default agent - inbound messages have nowhere to go until you pick one.
channelsPanel.pairingApprovalHint: A new sender is held until you approve them, so the agent will not reply to someone you have not approved yet.
channelsPanel.senderGuideIntro: This applies to every channel: WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Teams, Instagram/Messenger, X and email. The agent only answers people you have approved. You are not notified when someone new writes in, so check the queue after connecting a channel.
channelsPanel.senderGuideStep1: A new person messages your connected channel. They receive one reply with a pairing code. Their later messages are not answered and are not replayed after approval.
channelsPanel.senderGuideStep2: Open Contacts, find them under Pending approval, and approve or reject. Match the pairing code if you are unsure who it is.
channelsPanel.senderGuideStep3: Once approved, the agent answers their next message. If their pairing reply never arrived, check Approvals: outbound sends can need approval too.
channelsPanel.senderGuideModes: Prefer not to approve each person? In Contacts, set a channel to auto-approve new senders. Only do that for channels where anyone writing in is acceptable.
channelsPanel.voiceSubtitle: Real-time phone agent over your Twilio number
channelsPanel.voiceNeedsTwilioHint: Voice reuses your Twilio connection - connect Twilio on the WhatsApp card above, then come back here to route calls.
channelsPanel.dtmfMenuHint: Map keypad digits to agents. Pressing a mapped digit mid-call switches the agent for the rest of that call only - it doesn't change who answers new calls.

customCodeTools.pageSubtitle: Write a small Java or Python program and every agent in this workspace can call it as a tool.
customCodeTools.explainerSandbox: Your program runs in an isolated sandbox: no network access, no filesystem, and no access to platform or workspace data. It only ever sees the input the model passes it.
customCodeTools.explainerAdmin: Only workspace admins can create or change these. Everyone else sees them read-only.
customCodeTools.explainerToolName: The model calls your program by its tool name, and decides when to call it by reading the description you write - so write that description for the model, not for a person.
customCodeTools.loadError: Could not load custom code tools.
customCodeTools.readOnlyBody: Custom code tools can only be created or changed by a workspace admin. Ask an admin in your workspace if you need one added or fixed.
customCodeTools.disabledBody: This deployment was started without the code sandbox, so there's nothing to run your program in yet. An operator needs to enable it and restart the platform.
customCodeTools.emptyReadOnlyBody: Nobody in this workspace has added one. A workspace admin can create the first.
customCodeTools.toolNameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, 3-64 characters. This is the name the model calls, and it can't be changed once the tool is created.
customCodeTools.toolNameImmutableNote: Tool names can't be changed after the tool is created - agents may already be calling this one.
customCodeTools.toolNameInvalid: Tool name must start with a lowercase letter and use only lowercase letters, digits and underscores, 3-64 characters in total.
customCodeTools.descriptionPlaceholder: Looks up the delivery status of a customer order. Input needs an orderId.
customCodeTools.descriptionHelp: This is the text the AI model reads to decide when to call your tool. Be specific about what it does and what the input must contain.
customCodeTools.inputSchemaHelp: Leave blank for a generic object schema. When set, the model is shown these field names and types.
customCodeTools.outputDescriptionPlaceholder: Returns the order status and estimated delivery date.
customCodeTools.outputDescriptionHelp: Tells the model what it gets back, so it knows how to use the result.
customCodeTools.requiredFieldsError: Tool name, display name, description and code are all required.
customCodeTools.invalidSchemaError: The input schema isn't valid JSON.
customCodeTools.rejectedTitle: Saved, but this tool won't run yet
customCodeTools.rejectedBody: Your code was saved, so nothing is lost - but it didn't pass validation, so no agent can call it until it's fixed. The validator said:
customCodeTools.rejectedNoDetail: The validator rejected this code but didn't say why.
customCodeTools.testSaveFirst: Save the tool first - a test run executes the version stored on the server, not what's currently in the editor.
customCodeTools.toolCreatedSuccess: "{name}" created - agents can call it as a tool now.
customCodeTools.deleteDialogBody: This permanently removes the tool and its code. Any agent that calls {toolName} will stop being able to. This can't be undone.

customCodeTools.askAiPopoverSubtitle: Describe what the tool should do. Runs on-device when available, otherwise through your workspace's LLM - either way, the draft is checked in the sandbox before it lands in the editor.

customCodeTools.askAiRequirementRequired: Describe what the tool should do first.

customCodeTools.askAiGeneratedValidBody: Added to the editor below. Review it, then save when you're happy with it.
customCodeTools.askAiGeneratedInvalidBody: Added to the editor below anyway so nothing is lost - fix the issues, or regenerate.

skillsPage.pageSubtitle: Packaged expertise your agents load only when a task needs it.
skillsPage.howItWorks: A skill is a set of instructions for one kind of task. Agents see only each skill's name and description; when a request matches, the agent loads the full instructions, and reads any bundled files only if it needs them. So you can add many skills without slowing agents down or raising cost on unrelated chats.

providersPanel.description: Activate a provider with a real API key. Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Grok, Meta, Gemini, Google Vertex AI, Sarvam AI, E2B, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Ollama, local OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio), Mistral, DeepSeek, and Groq are fully implemented.

providersPanel.getStartedTitle: New to provider keys? Start here.
providersPanel.getStartedBody: Pick a provider below, create an API key on that provider's own site (each card's "How do I get this?" lists the exact steps), then paste it into the activation form and activate. Not sure which to pick first? OpenRouter or Gemini are good starting points. Prices, free tiers and trial credits change often - each card links to the provider's own pricing page for current details.
providersPanel.anthropicDesc: Claude models - the primary provider this platform is built and tested against.
providersPanel.openrouterDesc: One key, dozens of models from many labs (Claude, GPT, Llama, Grok, and more) via a single routing API.
providersPanel.metaDesc: Meta's Muse Spark models via the Meta Model API - 1M-token context, tool calling, images, video and PDFs.
providersPanel.geminiDesc: Google's Gemini models via a direct Google AI Studio API key - no GCP project required.
providersPanel.azureOpenaiDesc: GPT models via your own Azure OpenAI deployment.
providersPanel.googleVertexDesc: Gemini and other models via Google Cloud Vertex AI.
providersPanel.awsBedrockDesc: Claude, Titan, and other models via Amazon Bedrock.
providersPanel.ollamaDesc: Locally-hosted open models - no cloud API key required.
providersPanel.localOpenaiDesc: Run models on your own machine or network with vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio, Jan, LocalAI or any OpenAI-compatible server - no per-token cost, and your prompts stay on servers you run.
providersPanel.sarvamDesc: sarvam-30b/sarvam-105b chat models built for Indic languages - same key also powers translation (the 22 scheduled Indian languages), transliteration, language detection, speech-to-text, and text-to-speech. Language coverage differs by tool, and spoken replies on live calls are currently Indian English. Activating this key does NOT turn these tools on for every agent - go to the Agents page and attach Sarvam to whichever agents should use it, the same way you'd attach a knowledge base.
providersPanel.e2bDesc: Lets agents run short Python/Node/Bash snippets in a fresh, disposable sandbox and read back stdout/stderr - useful for verifying logic, running a calculation, or testing a script before an agent tells you it works. Not a chat provider - this key just unlocks the run_code tool. Activating it does NOT turn the tool on for every agent - go to the Agents page and attach E2B to whichever agents should use it, the same way you'd attach a knowledge base.
providersPanel.elevenLabsDesc: Lets agents speak replies aloud in your own cloned brand voice. Not a chat provider - this key just unlocks the speak tool. Activating it does NOT turn the tool on for every agent - go to the Agents page and attach voice to whichever agents should use it, the same way you'd attach a knowledge base.
providersPanel.mistralDesc: Mistral Large, Small, and Nemo models directly from Mistral AI.
providersPanel.deepseekDesc: DeepSeek Chat (V3) and DeepSeek Reasoner (R1) models directly from DeepSeek.
providersPanel.groqDesc: Open models (Llama, Gemma, and more) served on Groq's fast-inference cloud. Not the same company as Grok/xAI above - similar name, unrelated API.

onboardingTour.stepWelcomeBody: This console has four jobs, in the order you'll actually use them: get oriented, build, connect, and test. The floating orb in the corner is your nav - hover it any time to see every station.
onboardingTour.stepBuildBody: Agents are the AI personalities that answer chats - give one a system prompt (or click "Ask AI" next to that field to have it drafted for you) and a provider. Knowledge Base holds the .md/PDF/docs an agent can search before answering. Workflows chain agents, tools, and channels together on a visual canvas - most automations belong here, not in a single agent.
onboardingTour.stepConnectBody: Providers is where you activate an LLM (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) with your own API key - do this first, nothing else works without it. MCP Tools is a marketplace of extra capabilities (web search, databases, file access...) you can turn on for agents to use. Devices pairs a phone to let workflows control it directly.
onboardingTour.stepTestBody: Playground is a private chat window to try an agent before it's live. Once you're happy, connect it to WhatsApp, Telegram, or email from the Admin > Channels page so real customers can reach it.
onboardingTour.stepReadyBody: Every page also has a "?" Help button in the top-right that reopens this briefing or takes you to the full written guide with more detail on every screen.

helpPage.introHint: A complete walkthrough of every part of the console. New here? The welcome tour (the "?" button in the top right of any page) covers the short version - this page has the full detail.
helpPage.gettingStartedPara1: You don't need an API key to start: a hosted model is already included, and Free-tier agents run on the platform's shared pool automatically. If your plan allows your own provider, go to Connect → Providers, pick Anthropic, OpenAI, or another supported provider, and paste in your own API key from that provider's dashboard. The key is validated with a real (non-billed) call before it's saved, and encrypted at rest - once it shows ACTIVE, your agents use it instead of the hosted pool.
helpPage.gettingStartedPara2: After that, the natural build order is: create an Agent (Build → Agents), try it privately in the Playground (Test → Playground), then either wire it into a Workflow for multi-step automation, or connect it directly to a channel (WhatsApp, Telegram, email) so real people can talk to it.
helpPage.askAiPara1: Any field asking for a system prompt or description - an agent's system prompt, a knowledge collection's description, and more over time - has a small ✨ Ask AI button next to its label. Click it, describe what you want in a sentence (e.g. "a support agent that handles refunds and order status"), and it drafts the text using whichever LLM provider you've already activated. Nothing is applied automatically - you always review the suggestion and click Use this yourself, or Regenerate for another try.
helpPage.agentsPara1: An agent is one AI persona: a system prompt, an LLM provider/model, and optionally a knowledge base and a restricted set of tools. Start from a template (support triage, research assistant, etc.) to pre-fill a reasonable system prompt, or start from scratch and use Ask AI to draft one.
helpPage.agentsPara2: Tool access and knowledge access are both allow-lists: leave them empty for "unrestricted" (the agent can use anything currently available to your tenant), or check specific items to restrict the agent to only those. This matters for anything customer-facing - you generally don't want a public support bot to have access to every internal tool.
helpPage.knowledgePara1: Upload .md, PDF, Word, images (OCR), or audio/video (transcribed) files and they're chunked and embedded into a searchable vector store. Collections are folders you can nest and scope agents to - e.g. a "Returns Policy" collection only certain agents can search, versus a "Public FAQ" collection every agent can use.
helpPage.knowledgePara2: An agent only searches its knowledge base if "Attach knowledge base" is checked when creating it (or toggled on later from the Agents page), and only within whatever collections its knowledge-access allow-list permits.
helpPage.workflowsPara1: The visual canvas for multi-step automation: drag nodes (Trigger, Agent, Knowledge Search, Condition, Output, Device Control, and more) and connect them. Every node calls the real service behind it - a Workflow run genuinely calls your agent, genuinely searches your knowledge base, genuinely sends the WhatsApp message.
helpPage.workflowsPara2: Workflows can start three ways: manually (the "Run" button), on a schedule (cron expression, e.g. "every morning at 8am"), or via a webhook URL you can call from any external system. Every run is logged step-by-step under that workflow's Runs tab, including each individual tool call an Agent node made along the way.
helpPage.toolsPara1: A marketplace of Model Context Protocol servers and built-in tools an agent can call mid-conversation (web search, a database, the filesystem, your own custom scripts...). Enable the ones you want available, then scope which agents can actually use them from each agent's tool-access editor. Disabling a server here immediately removes it from every agent's available tools, even ones that previously had it checked.
helpPage.researchPara1: Where it is switched on, Research takes one question, runs several web searches, reads the most useful pages and writes a report. Each claim carries a marker such as [S1] that opens the source, and the Sources list shows the exact passage that was quoted. A run keeps going if you close the tab, and you can save the report as Markdown (PDF and Word on paid plans). Any agent can do the same in chat once Deep research is turned on in its Capabilities.
helpPage.researchPara2: Every run has limits, shown on the Research page before you start: a fixed number of web searches and page reads, a time limit for each research pass, and a number of runs per day. A report marked Partial hit one of those limits or could not read some pages. The citation check compares wording only - it confirms that a quote really appears in the source, not that the source itself is right, so read the sources for anything that matters.
helpPage.channelsPara1: Under Admin → Channels: connect WhatsApp either through Twilio (fast sandbox setup, small per-message fee) or directly through Meta's own WhatsApp Business Platform (no middleman fee, more setup - your own Meta App, System User token, and App Secret). If both are configured, the direct Meta connection is used automatically.
helpPage.channelsPara2: The first time a new phone number messages in, it shows up under Pending sender pairings and needs to be approved before your agents will hold a live conversation with it - this stops a stranger messaging your number from getting an unattended AI conversation by default.
helpPage.devicesPara1: Pair a phone (Android or iOS) to your tenant from the Devices page, and a workflow's Device Control node can tap, type, open apps on, or screenshot it. Android supports full automation via Android's Accessibility Service; iOS is limited by Apple's own sandboxing to opening apps only - see the Mobile SDK's CONSTRAINTS.md for the full, honest breakdown of what each platform can and can't do.
helpPage.adminPara1: Users: invite teammates and assign roles (only a tenant-admin can change roles or credentials). Approvals is the human-in-the-loop inbox - any action your guardrail policy flags as needing sign-off (e.g. an agent about to send a WhatsApp message) waits here until approved or rejected. Audit Log is a complete, append-only record of every significant action taken in your tenant, by a person or an agent.
helpPage.faqPara1: "No active providers yet" when creating an agent - you should not see this on a new account: every new account runs on the platform's hosted pool for its first 3 months, and the Free plan does after that. It appears once you are on a paid plan using your own provider - activate one under Connect → Providers.
helpPage.faqPara2: Ask AI button gives an error - same cause as above. It only fails when your account is off the hosted pool and has no active provider of its own.
helpPage.faqPara3: A pending WhatsApp/Telegram sender never gets a reply - check Admin → Channels for a pairing waiting on your approval.
helpPage.faqPara4: A tool doesn't show up for an agent - confirm it's enabled under MCP Tools, and that the agent's tool-access list either includes it or is left empty (unrestricted).

landing.atlas_title: Every capability, on one screen. Search it.
landing.atlas_sub: Thirty-six things your free account opens on day one — each one shipped and counted in the code that runs this page. Tap any tile for the detail, and where it lives in the console.
landing.atlas_empty: Nothing matches. Try a shorter word — or ask us, we answer.
landing.atlas_ctaSignup: Open all of it — create free account
landing.atlas_note: Every account that registers has everything unlocked for its first 3 months. Opt-in items are switches, not extra charges.
landing.atlas_vision_body: Send a photo, a scanned bill or a screenshot in any chat and it reads what is in it — up to three files, 10 MB in total per message, on every model that supports images.
landing.atlas_vision_where: Console → Playground → attach; any channel that carries images.
landing.atlas_hearing_body: Voice notes and live phone calls are transcribed as they happen, with an on-device Whisper option that keeps audio on your hardware.
landing.atlas_hearing_where: Console → Channels → Voice; push-to-talk in the Playground.
landing.atlas_voice_body: Spoken replies on calls and in the console, in the customer's own language, with Indian-language voices.
landing.atlas_voice_where: Console → Channels → Voice; the speaker button in any chat.
landing.atlas_docs_body: Price lists, contracts, manuals, scanned paper. It searches them by meaning and by keyword — 5 embedding models, OCR for scanned pages, 23 search languages.
landing.atlas_models_body: Bring your own key across 14 providers, use the hosted pool free, or switch models per agent whenever you like. Failover is automatic.
landing.atlas_edge_body: 28 curated models run inside the browser on WebGPU — no server, no key, and the data never leaves the device. Falls back to the hosted pool only if you allow it.
landing.atlas_edge_where: Console → Browser models; the device toggle in any chat.
landing.atlas_memory_body: Every agent remembers its own conversations. Flip one switch and what it learns goes into a shared graph the rest of your team's agents can recall — isolated per workspace.
landing.atlas_memory_where: Console → Agents → Memory → share with workspace.
landing.atlas_learning_body: Experimental, and off by default. A thumbs-up, a rating or an edit on a reply can be recorded as a reward, and an admin can switch on a per-agent policy that tries different model routes and favours the ones that score better. Nothing runs until an admin enables a policy and sets its options.
landing.atlas_learning_where: Console → Agents → Learning; admin policies per agent.
landing.atlas_tools_body: Web search and fetch, HTTP and OpenAPI calls, Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets, YouTube, UPI payment links, documents, images, code execution, translation and more — each gated by the same approval and guardrail layer.
landing.atlas_mcp_body: 17 curated MCP servers (5 need no credentials at all), any other MCP server you point it at, and an indexed catalog of 18,000+ registry entries. VegaDūta is an MCP server itself, so other AI clients can call your agents.
landing.atlas_selftools_body: No integration for what you need? It reads the code, writes a new tool, tests it in a sandbox, and uses it — behind an approval gate.
landing.atlas_media_body: Prompt-to-image inside any agent or the live studio, and short generated video clips on paid plans — with industry-tailored prompts to start from.
landing.atlas_media_where: Live studio on this page; any agent with image generation on.
landing.atlas_channels_body: WhatsApp (Meta Cloud API or Twilio), Telegram, Email, voice calls, Slack, Discord, Instagram, Messenger and X — one agent, one conversation memory across all of them.
landing.atlas_share_body: Publish an agent or a workflow as a public link. Anyone can run it from a phone — no app, no login — within limits you set.
landing.atlas_share_where: Console → Agents → Share; the live studio's publish step.
landing.atlas_a2a_body: A published A2A agent card other agents can discover and call, AG-UI streaming runs, and a REST API of 600+ endpoints behind everything you can click.
landing.atlas_guardrails_body: Six guardrail types check what goes in and what comes out — PII, profanity, toxicity, jailbreak and prompt injection, policy — plus your own workspace rules, with an off switch you control.
landing.atlas_approvals_body: Set an agent's autonomy tier and every consequential action waits in your approval queue before it fires. Routine work just happens.
landing.atlas_quality_body: Six automated judges score real runs — accuracy, helpfulness, relevance, tone, safety and length — so “the AI did something odd” becomes a number you can watch and a run you can replay.
landing.atlas_audit_body: Every action, every tool call, every approval — who, what, when — in a log you can read, export and hand to an auditor.
landing.atlas_budgets_body: A daily budget per user, rate limits per workspace and plan limits that are enforced in code, not on a slide. No surprise bills.
landing.atlas_workflows_body: Lay out a process with 35 node types — schedules, webhooks and event triggers, branches, loops, parallel fan-out, approvals, bulk email and CRM steps. Expressions pass values between steps, and pinned data lets you rebuild one step without re-running the rest.
landing.atlas_magic_body: One sentence in. It analyses intent, searches the MCP registry, picks a model from the live pool, builds a working agent and publishes a share link — no signup, right on this page.
landing.atlas_magic_where: The live studio, further down this page.
landing.atlas_templates_body: Share a working agent or workflow with everyone; install one in a click. Every submission is reviewed by a human before it is listed.
landing.atlas_academy_body: 280+ free lessons from the first agent to expert operations, in Indian languages as well as English, with certificates for learners who finish.
landing.atlas_academy_where: academy.vegaduta.ai — free, no account needed to start.
landing.atlas_codeintel_body: Point it at a repository. It maps callers and callees, checks blast radius before an edit, works in a sandboxed workspace and shows you the diff before anything merges.
landing.atlas_codeintel_where: Console → Code; VS Code and JetBrains plugins.
landing.atlas_plugins_body: VS Code and JetBrains plugins chat with agents, run workflows and offer inline explain / fix / refactor on selected code. The Chrome extension is a side-panel agent that follows you across the web, with one-click “ask about this selection”.
landing.atlas_plugins_where: Plugins page (first-party builds, checksum-verified); the Chrome extension is in Web Store review.
landing.atlas_mobile_body: Chat, quick tasks, workflows and approvals on your phone, with on-device AI on capable devices. Currently a beta build you download directly.
landing.atlas_security_body: Keycloak sign-in (OIDC, PKCE), AES-encrypted provider keys and channel secrets, one isolated database schema per workspace, full export and erasure on request.
landing.atlas_security_where: Every account, from the first minute.
landing.atlas_touch_body: Web Bluetooth is live for on-device models: an agent running in your browser (Chromium, HTTPS) can read a paired sensor with no server involved. A server-side agent cannot borrow your radio yet — that relay is designed, not built.

landing.h3_h1Em: Ship the agent — and the app around it.

VegaDūta builds the agent, picks its tools and model, connects it to WhatsApp, voice, email and six more channels — and now builds the phone app your customers use to reach it. Risky steps wait for your approval, and every action lands in the audit log.
landing.h2_w_sales_brief: Every new website lead goes into the CRM — email them within the hour, follow up in three days if they are quiet, and flag every reply and bounce.
landing.sh_title: Six new jobs it learned this month.
landing.sh_sub: No roadmap slides. Everything below is live on vegaduta.ai today: shipped, not promised.
landing.sh_app_title: Say the app. Hold it in your hand.
landing.sh_app_body: Describe an app and App Studio builds a multi-page phone app you can preview live, with camera, Bluetooth, vibration and sharing. Plug in your own agents and workflows without writing a backend, then publish it with its own sign-in for your customers.

landing.h4_lead: Say what you need in plain English. VegaDūta builds the agent, picks its tools and model, and puts it on WhatsApp, voice, email and six more channels. Then it shows its work: replay any run step by step, test a change before customers see it, and approve the risky steps yourself. It builds the phone app around the agent too.
landing.sx_title: Six ways it got easier to trust this month.
landing.sx_sub: Building an agent takes a sentence. Knowing it will behave takes evidence. Everything below is live in VegaDūta today.
landing.sx_lab_title: See exactly why it said that.
landing.sx_lab_body: Agent Lab draws any past run as a graph of every model call and tool call. Re-run it from the step you choose, remove parts of the prompt to see which ones the answer depends on, and repeat an input to check that it answers the same way twice.
landing.sx_skills_title: Skills it picks up only when it needs them.
landing.sx_skills_body: Fourteen built-in skills, from customer support and SQL to Word, Excel and PDF files, each a plain SKILL.md folder. An agent reads the full instructions only when a task calls for them. It can also draft new skills from its own successful runs, and those stay off until an admin approves them.
landing.sx_teams_title: One lead, a team behind it.
landing.sx_teams_body: Give an agent two or more specialist colleagues and it splits a job between them at the same time, then combines the answers. Delegation goes one level deep, each branch has a time limit, and the whole team shares one run budget.
landing.sx_flow_body: Pin a step's output while you build, so the steps after it run on the same data. Expressions pass values between steps, draft runs stay separate from production, and long jobs run in the background while you do something else.
landing.sx_evals_title: A new version has to earn Production.
landing.sx_evals_body: Score an agent against your own test set with six automated judges, with confidence intervals so one lucky run doesn't fool you. Set a pass bar, and a version that falls short is not promoted.
landing.sx_memory_body: One page lists what your agents have learned about you. Edit what is wrong, delete what you don't want kept, and write the notes you want every conversation to start with.

An agent can hand off to exactly one specialist colleague — one hop, by design — so there's no runaway chain of agents delegating to each other.
