landing.earnPage_lede: There has never been a bigger gap between what businesses need and who can build it. Agentic AI closes that gap — and the people who learn it first get to be the ones businesses pay. This page is the honest playbook: what to learn, what it costs, how to deliver, and how to price.

landing.earnPage_studentStat: In a 2026 Florida Tech survey, 39% of Gen Z workers already use AI to earn side income — most start small ($1–$999/month), and it compounds with skill. Honest numbers, not guru promises:
landing.earnPage_playbookSub: From zero to your first paying business customer.
landing.earnPage_s1Body: The Academy takes you from "what is an agent?" to shipping production workflows — 100+ lessons, hands-on labs, in plain language. No code needed to start; a real REST API, webhooks and MCP when you're ready to go deep. No card, no catch.
landing.earnPage_s2Body: One subscription gives you the factory: agents on WhatsApp, Email, Slack, Phone and Telegram, 100+ tool integrations, human-approval controls and a full audit log. Bring your own keys for frontier models — OpenAI, Gemini, Claude and more — so you control cost and capability, or start on the built-in model pool for free.
landing.earnPage_s3Body: Start local and specific: the shop that misses WhatsApp orders after 9pm, the clinic drowning in appointment calls, the coaching class that never follows up. Browse 248 ready-to-run workflow recipes across 89 industries to see what a first project looks like — then pick ONE business and ONE workflow.
landing.earnPage_s4Body: Describe the agent in a sentence and watch it build in Magic Studio, then harden it: ground it in the client's documents, set approval rules so nothing risky happens without a human, and hand the owner an audit log of every decision. Trust is the product — the automation is just how you deliver it.
landing.earnPage_s5Title: 5 · Price the outcome, not your hours
landing.earnPage_s5Body: The old model bills time; the new model shares value. Measure what the agent actually does for the business — orders captured, hours saved, customers answered at 2am — put a number on it, and charge a fraction of that number every month. A setup fee plus an outcome-linked retainer is the pattern the best AI businesses use.
landing.earnPage_mathSub: An illustrative example — your numbers will differ, and that's the point: you measure them.
landing.earnPage_mathStep1: A shop misses ~20 orders a month outside opening hours. Average order ₹400 / $10 — that's real revenue walking away.
landing.earnPage_mathStep2: Your agent answers every channel 24/7 and captures even half of them: measurable new revenue every month, plus hours of answering repeated questions returned to the owner.
landing.earnPage_mathStep3: You charge a setup fee plus a monthly retainer that stays well below the value created — the owner profits from day one, and your revenue recurs. Ten clients like this is a real company.
landing.earnPage_mathNote: No invented success stories here — this is arithmetic, not a testimonial. The engagement dashboard and audit log give you the real numbers to show your client every month.

landing.sdlc_title: Agents that actually know your codebase
landing.sdlc_sub: Not keyword search dressed up as intelligence — your agents query a real AST-parsed map of your repo, trace the blast radius of a change, and execute inside an isolated workspace that never moves without your sign-off.
landing.sdlc_bullet1Lead: Ask it “what calls this?” and get a real answer.
landing.sdlc_bullet1Body: Code search runs on tree-sitter AST chunking, not fuzzy text matching — agents can trace callers, callees, and the full impact graph of a function before anyone touches it.
landing.sdlc_bullet2Lead: Agents can run code, not just suggest it.
landing.sdlc_bullet2Body: A dedicated workspace/execution loop lets an agent create an isolated git worktree, run your code, apply a fix, and diff the result — the same run → fail → apply → rerun cycle a human would use.
landing.sdlc_bullet3Lead: Every run and every apply is a checkpoint, not a rubber stamp.
landing.sdlc_bullet3Body: Executing code and applying changes each sit behind their own human-approval gate — the agent proposes, you approve, nothing lands unattended.
landing.sdlc_bullet4Body: The same code intelligence is reachable over MCP, so it's not locked to VegaDūta's built-in agents — plug it into whatever agent tooling you already run.
landing.sdlc_card1_title: “Where does this happen?” — answered from your code graph
landing.sdlc_card1_body: Semantic code search plus real caller/callee and blast-radius tools (search_code, code_callers, code_impact). Ask in Slack, get file:line citations — or an honest “not found”, never a plausible guess.
landing.sdlc_card2_title: PR review routed to specialist reviewers
landing.sdlc_card2_body: A supervisor reads per-file summaries and wakes only the specialists a PR needs — security, data/migrations, API contract. Each one checks real call sites before commenting. The agent comments; it never approves or merges.
landing.sdlc_card3_title: Run code in a disposable sandbox
landing.sdlc_card3_body: The run_code tool executes short Python, Node or Bash snippets in a fresh E2B sandbox and reads back stdout/stderr — so an agent verifies logic actually works before telling you it does.
landing.sdlc_card4_title: Dependency & CVE bumps, approved diff by diff
landing.sdlc_card4_body: code_callers separates “in the lockfile” from “actually reachable from our code”. The minimal bump is prepared and test-proven in an isolated workspace — and a human approves each repo's exact diff before anything lands.
landing.sdlc_card5_title: Release notes from the real commit range
landing.sdlc_card5_body: The tag range — not memory — sets the scope. Breaking changes are verified against actual callers via code_impact, grouped by audience, and held at an approval gate: the agent drafts, a human publishes.
landing.sdlc_card6_body: Nightly failures are triaged one by one — flake, environment or real break — with the root cause traced to a suspect file. Flake fixes are drafted in a sandbox and re-run N times to prove stability before any human reviews the PR.
landing.sdlc_footerNote: GitHub and GitLab are reached the honest way — through MCP servers from the registry (open PRs, review diffs, file issues), not a bolt-on you have to trust blindly. Eight ready-to-adapt recipes show the full builds: agents, tools, guardrails and cost tiers.
landing.platform_sub: How a brief becomes a real outcome — the pipeline, the approval gate, where it thinks, what it can reach, and how far it can delegate. Every line maps to shipped code, not a roadmap slide.
landing.platform_row1_title: The nervous system: brief → plan → action → outcome
landing.platform_row1_body: Every request runs through the same real pipeline — understand the brief, plan the steps, call the right tool, log the result. It's not a canned script, and it's the same execution path whether the channel is WhatsApp, email or a live phone call.
landing.platform_row2_title: You approve the calls that matter
landing.platform_row2_body: Every side-effecting step queues through a human-approval gate before it fires — with one honest exception: a live voice reply is spoken in the moment, not queued, because a phone call can't pause mid-sentence for a click.
landing.platform_row3_body: Run inference on-device for free, bring your own model key, or use the platform's shared pool. Same agent, same behavior — just a different address for the thinking.
landing.platform_row5_title: One hop to a specialist, by design
landing.platform_row5_body: An agent can hand off to one specialist colleague — one hop, by design. That colleague can't hand off again, so there's no runaway chain of agents delegating to each other.
landing.platform_p1_body: Nine native channel adapters feed one shared session, memory and approval pipeline — the same agent, with the same context, everywhere your customers already are.
landing.platform_p1_pt1: WhatsApp two ways — Meta Cloud API or Twilio — with outbound auto-routed to whichever connection is active.
landing.platform_p1_pt2: Voice calls and SMS on Twilio: live spoken replies over Twilio Conversation Relay, with per-caller memory that persists from call to call.
landing.platform_p1_pt3: Telegram, Slack, Discord, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, X (Twitter) DMs and email — native, webhook-verified adapters, not third-party glue.
landing.platform_p2_body: The entire official MCP registry — 18,000+ servers — is indexed into an instantly searchable catalog. Filesystem, fetch and browser-automation servers activate in one click; GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Postgres and Brave Search get an encrypted credential form.
landing.platform_p2_pt1: Each connected server runs as its own isolated process with a scrubbed environment — platform secrets are never handed to it.
landing.platform_p2_pt2: Defense in depth on every launch: launcher allowlist, blocked code-eval flags, SSRF-guarded URLs, per-tenant process caps.
landing.platform_p2_pt3: Connections are tenant-scoped, health-checked every five minutes, and reconnected automatically when a server drops.
landing.platform_p3_title: Experimental: agents that learn from feedback
landing.platform_p3_body: An experimental feedback-learning loop, off by default and opt-in per agent, can adjust model routing, prompt variants and tool subsets from feedback. Until you switch it on, your agent keeps its exact configured behavior.
landing.platform_p3_pt1: It is a preview feature that has not been proven in production, so treat it as an experiment, not a guarantee of better results.
landing.platform_p3_pt2: Every thumbs-up, rating or edit becomes training signal for the exact configuration that produced that answer.
landing.platform_p3_pt3: Your preference data exports as DPO pairs or KTO samples whenever you want to fine-tune offline. It stays yours.

landing.h5_lead: Describe the job in plain English. VegaDūta builds the agent, picks its tools and model, and puts it on WhatsApp, voice, email and six more channels. You set the rules: approve the risky steps, fence what it can touch, test every change before a customer sees it. It shows the proof: every run recorded step by step, replayable down to the last tool call.

landing.faqA1FreeMode: Yes — free during our launch. Every feature is unlocked: agents, workflows and seats, WhatsApp, Telegram and Email, white-label branding. Pricing will be introduced later to sustain the infrastructure and the team, with advance notice; until then you are free to explore, experiment and run. landing.whySwitch_title: Not another node-based builder, or a one-off AI app generator
landing.whySwitch_sub: Tools like n8n and no-code AI app builders are great at what they're built for. VegaDūta is built for a different job: give a real business a real agent, live on the channels its customers already use.
landing.whySwitch_p1_contrast: Generic workflow builders give you nodes and connectors — you still have to build and host your own channel integration before a single customer can actually talk to it.
landing.whySwitch_p2_us: One prompt becomes an agent, a workflow, AND a deployed channel
landing.whySwitch_p2_contrast: A no-code AI app builder gets you a hosted app or a chat window. Here, the same sentence creates a real agent with tools, a workflow behind it, and a live number your customers can message today.
landing.whySwitch_p3_us: Guardrails and a real workflow engine, included
landing.whySwitch_p3_contrast: Most builders leave moderation, approval gates and retries as something you assemble yourself out of extra nodes. This platform runs on a Temporal-backed engine with policy-pack guardrails from day one.
landing.faq_q1: Is the Free plan actually free?
landing.faq_a1: Yes — ₹0/$0, no card. Every feature is unlocked for 3 months for everyone who registers; after that you land on the Free plan, which is a real plan and not a countdown: 5 agents, 3 workflows, 2 seats, WhatsApp, Telegram and Email, and a hosted model included (30 messages/day) so your first agent answers without an API key.
landing.faq_q2: Do I need my own OpenAI or Gemini API key?
landing.faq_a2: No. Every plan includes the platform's pooled hosted model, so your first agent works with zero setup. On paid plans you can bring your own key for any supported provider — including Sarvam for Indian languages — and your agents switch to it.
landing.faq_q3: Can it really answer my business WhatsApp?
landing.faq_a3: Yes, on every plan including Free — you connect your own number via Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API or Twilio, and the agent answers there directly. We do not charge for the channel; the number and any Meta conversation fees stay yours. The conversations playing on this page are clearly-labelled simulations of that experience.
landing.faq_q4: What languages does it work in?
landing.faq_a4: All 22 scheduled Indian languages plus English and more — the console itself ships in 30 languages, and agents reply in the language the customer writes in. Voice in and out is available too, in the languages your chosen speech provider supports.
landing.faq_q5: What if the AI does something it shouldn't?
landing.faq_a5: You decide how much rope it gets. Set an agent's autonomy tier so consequential actions wait in your approval queue instead of just happening, guardrails and content moderation are built in, and every action lands in an audit log you can review any time.
landing.faq_q6: I've never built anything with AI. Where do I start?
landing.faq_a6: Two free paths: the live studio on this page builds something real from one sentence with no signup, and the VegaDūta Academy — 100+ free lessons with hands-on labs — takes you from zero to your first working agent.

landing.pw_eyebrow: Models, providers and where they run
landing.pw_title: Bring your own key. Use ours. Or run it on your own machine.
landing.pw_sub: The brain is not welded in. Every agent you build can point at a provider you pay directly, at the model pool we host for free, or at a model that never leaves your laptop — and you can change your mind later without rebuilding the agent.
landing.pw_door1_body: The model runs in your browser on WebGPU, and the router never calls a server to produce the answer.
landing.pw_door2_body: {count} language-model providers you can connect with your own account and your own billing.
landing.pw_door3_body: The free plan's hosted model — 30 messages a day, no API key, nothing to configure.
landing.pw_device_title: A model that never leaves the machine you are sitting at.
landing.pw_device_body: Switch on on-device mode and the weights are downloaded once into your browser, then answers are generated locally on WebGPU. Chrome's own built-in model can be used the same way. When a turn is too big for the device, it escalates to the cloud instead of failing.
landing.pw_device_weights: We do not host or train these models. WebLLM pulls the weights from the upstream MLC / Hugging Face CDN, and nothing downloads or runs on your device until you turn it on.
landing.pw_p_webllm: Open models compiled for WebGPU, running inside the browser tab.
landing.pw_p_chromeAi: Chrome's built-in on-device model, used when the browser offers it.
landing.pw_code_title: Yes — a model on your own device can write tool code for you.
landing.pw_code_sub: This is the part people do not believe, so here is exactly how far it goes and exactly where it stops. Both columns describe the same feature.
landing.pw_code_does1: Ask AI in Custom Code Tools drafts a tool on your device — one self-contained Java class or Python module, sandboxed with no file, network or process access.
landing.pw_code_does2: The platform re-checks that code before you keep it. The device is never trusted to certify its own output, and a check that fails to run counts as a failure, not a pass.
landing.pw_code_does3: An on-device model gets the same tools a cloud model gets. It proposes the call; the server executes it through the same approval gate, step ceiling and audit log.
landing.pw_code_does4: For real repository work, proposed file changes land in a scratch workspace and wait for a tenant admin to approve them — then you read the unified diff of exactly what landed.
landing.pw_code_does5: If a turn is too big for your device, it escalates to the cloud instead of failing.
landing.pw_code_never1: It never writes to your repository or your branch. The workspace is a throwaway clone and nothing is ever pushed back.
landing.pw_code_never2: It never opens a pull request. No part of this platform creates one.
landing.pw_code_never3: It never reads your codebase itself. Code search runs on the server against an index, and the device only sees the passages that come back.
landing.pw_code_never4: It never runs your builds or tests on its own. Those execute server-side, only after approval, and never hand their output straight back to the model.
landing.pw_code_never5: It is never the default. On-device needs an explicit opt-in and weights you have already chosen to download.
landing.pw_code_footnote: Code-workspace tools stay off until you switch them on for a specific agent, and that agent needs an explicit repository grant — an empty grant denies everything.
landing.pw_g_llmNote: Every one of these is configurable today. None of them is a coming-soon card.
landing.pw_note_byok: Connecting your own key is a Premium capability. On the Free plan you do not need one at all — every agent routes through our shared hosted pool, 30 messages a day, with nothing to configure.
landing.pw_g_voiceNote: Listening and speaking are separate from the brain — choose them per agent.
landing.pw_note_attach: Adding a key does not switch these on everywhere. You attach voice or transcription to the specific agents that should have it, the same way you attach a knowledge base — and ElevenLabs needs at least one cloned voice before it can speak.
landing.pw_p_anthropic: Claude models on your own Anthropic key — the provider this platform is built and tested against.
landing.pw_p_openai: GPT models via your OpenAI account, also used for image generation.
landing.pw_p_gemini: Google's Gemini models on a direct AI Studio key. No GCP project needed.
landing.pw_p_vertex: Gemini and more through your own Google Cloud project — text, images and video.
landing.pw_p_azure: GPT models served from your own Azure OpenAI deployment and region.
landing.pw_p_bedrock: Models served through your Amazon Bedrock account and IAM credentials.
landing.pw_p_openrouter: One key, many labs. Routes to dozens of models through a single API.
landing.pw_p_mistral: Mistral's own models, on a key from Mistral AI.
landing.pw_p_deepseek: DeepSeek's own models, on a key from DeepSeek.
landing.pw_p_groq: Open models served on Groq's fast-inference cloud. A different company from Grok.
landing.pw_p_meta: Muse Spark models directly from Meta, on a Meta Model API key.
landing.pw_p_sarvam: Chat models built for Indic languages — one key also covers translation, transliteration and language detection across 22 Indian languages.
landing.pw_p_ollama: Point an agent at open models you host yourself. Your server, your network, no cloud key.
landing.pw_p_sarvamVoice: Speech-to-text and text-to-speech on your Sarvam key. Spoken replies on live calls are currently Indian English; the speak tool can ask for another language.
landing.pw_p_elevenlabs: Agents speak replies aloud in a voice you have cloned in your own ElevenLabs account.
landing.pw_p_whisper: Self-hosted faster-whisper running on our own sidecar. Transcription with no key and no vendor.
landing.pw_p_openaiWhisper: Video-to-text using the OpenAI key you have already connected.
landing.pw_p_e2b: Short Python, Node or Bash snippets in a fresh disposable sandbox. Not a chat provider — this key unlocks the run_code tool.
landing.pw_p_embeddings: Five local sentence-transformers models power your knowledge base. Embeddings run on CPU here, never through a paid hosted API.
landing.pw_closing: One platform, three places to think, and no lock-in in any direction. Start on the free hosted model, move to your own key when it pays for itself, and pull a model onto your own device the day that matters more than speed.

hire.faq_q1: Do I need an API key to start?
hire.faq_a1: No. The Free plan includes a hosted model — sign up and your agent answers within minutes. Growing teams can bring their own key from any of 14 providers and the platform routes across them.
hire.faq_q2: Will it say something wrong to my customers?
hire.faq_a2: It answers from your documents with cited sources, inside guardrails you set, and consequential actions wait in the approval queue for your stamp. Every reply is recorded — see Clause 1.
hire.faq_q3: What stops the AI bill from exploding?
hire.faq_a3: Clause 2 is real software: hard daily spend caps per user and per feature, with a platform-wide master switch on top. At the cap, spending stops.
hire.faq_a4: Yes — through the official routes (Twilio, or Meta's Cloud API with embedded signup), starting on the Premium plan. Free-plan agents work on Telegram and email.
hire.faq_q5: I'm not technical. Honestly, can I do this?
hire.faq_a5: Answer two interview questions and the agent assembles itself; or start from 29 ready-made templates and 248 industry playbooks. The free Academy — 127 lessons, 12 hands-on labs — is ungated: seekho pehle, decide baad mein.
hire.faq_q6: Why should I trust a new company?
hire.faq_a6: Don't — verify. Every number on this page is countable in the product; the pledge at the top lists what we refuse to do; the free plan means you risk $0 and no card to find out. Trust is the product's job, not this page's.

relay.title: Answer my channels from this device
relay.lead: Turn this browser into the model behind your SMS and WhatsApp numbers. While it is on, inbound messages on the channels you pick are answered here, on-device, and sent back through the usual approval gate. No API key, no GPU server, no per-token cost. When this tab is closed or busy for too long, the hosted model answers instead.

market.title: Model marketplace
market.subtitle: One-time downloads that then run free and private in your browser.
market.noFit: May be slow or fail on this device
market.unverified: Memory can't be checked in this browser - set your RAM above to confirm
market.purposeBuiltin: Instant everyday replies, built into your browser
market.purposeText: Chat and text replies, fully on-device
market.purposeVision: Camera and image understanding, fully on-device
market.purposeStt: Turns your speech into text, fully on-device
market.purposeTts: Speaks replies out loud, fully on-device
market.purposeMotion: Smooth motion for Clip Studio videos, rendered in your browser

market.motionDetail: Turns still images into smooth motion clips. Downloads automatically the first time you use Motion+ in Clip Studio.

installed.title: Installed on this device
installed.subtitle: Everything below lives in this browser's storage and runs offline.
installed.empty: Nothing installed yet — pick a model from the marketplace above.
installed.deleteConfirm: Remove {model} from this device? You can download it again anytime.
installed.storage: Storage: {used} used of {quota} available for this site

dataShield.title: Strip personal data before a turn leaves this device
dataShield.body: When a turn is too big for your device and falls back to a hosted model, this device masks the sensitive parts first. The masking happens in your browser — the real values never travel.
dataShield.optionOffDetail: Send the message exactly as written. Agents with tenant guardrails are still scrubbed.
dataShield.optionSecretsDetail: Recommended. Masks payment card and government ID numbers, which a hosted model never needs to do the work.
dataShield.optionContactDetail: Stronger, but it changes what some tasks can do — "draft a reply to jane@acme.com" loses the address.
dataShield.optionModelDetail: Uses an on-device model to find what patterns can't. Only runs when a model is already loaded; it never starts a download.
dataShield.modelReady: On-device masking is active — a model is loaded and ready.
dataShield.modelIdle: No model is loaded right now, so this level behaves like the one above it until one is.

browserTools.title: Let browser agents use this agent's tools
browserTools.body: Publishes this agent's approved tools to the browser as typed tools (WebMCP), so an AI agent running in your browser can call them directly instead of guessing at the page. Every call still goes through the same approval and audit rules as always.
browserTools.unsupported: This browser doesn't support the browser tool API yet. Chrome is the only one that does today — everything else is unaffected.
browserTools.testing: Running on Chrome's experimental flag, not the shipped API.
browserTools.none: Nothing published yet — open an agent to publish its tools.

privacy.title: Your device, your data
privacy.body: On-device models run entirely in your browser: prompts, files and camera frames never leave this device, and replies cost nothing. If a task is too big for your device, it falls back to hosted models only according to the setting you chose above — and Hosted only means exactly that.

localCode.title: Local code
localCode.subtitle: Ask questions about a folder on this device and apply the edits it suggests. The code is read inside your browser and never uploaded.

unsupported.title: This browser can't open a folder
unsupported.body: Reading a folder from your device needs the File System Access API, and this browser doesn't have it. Nothing is broken — there is simply nothing this page can do here.
unsupported.hint: Chrome, Edge and other desktop Chromium browsers support it today. Safari and Firefox don't yet.

model.notReadyTitle: No on-device model is ready yet
model.notReadyBody: Answers here run entirely on your machine, so a model has to be installed first. This page never starts a download on its own — choose and download one in the Edge console, then come back.
model.edgeOffTitle: On-device AI is off in this build
model.edgeOffBody: Answering runs only on your machine, and on-device AI is switched off for this deployment — so there is no model this page could ask, and no hosted one it is willing to fall back to. Opening and indexing a folder still work; asking does not.

repo.title: Open a folder
repo.body: Choose the project you want to ask about. Your browser asks for permission first, and you can withdraw it at any time.
repo.stayHere: Files stay on this device — nothing is uploaded.
repo.noCodeFiles: No code files found in this folder. Try one closer to the source.
repo.capped: Stopped after the first {count} files — this index covers part of the folder, not all of it.
repo.skipped: Skipped {large} files that were too large and {unreadable} this browser couldn't read.
repo.rememberedHint: You opened this folder before. Your browser drops folder access on reload, so reopening asks for permission again.
repo.reopenFailed: That folder couldn't be reopened — it may have moved, been renamed, or had permission refused. Open it again below.

index.restored: An index of {files} files ({chunks} chunks) from an earlier visit is still on this device — you can ask questions now, or open the folder again to refresh it.
index.needEmbedder: Searching your code needs a small embedding model on this device, and it isn't here yet. Nothing downloads until you press the button below.
index.enableEmbedderHint: Downloads the embedding model that turns your files into a searchable index. It happens once on this device, only when you press this, and the model never leaves it.
index.installFailedUnknown: setup didn't finish, and no reason was reported
index.installCancelled: Cancelled — local search isn't set up on this device.
index.installedNow: Local search is ready on this device.
index.embedderOff: On-device AI is switched off for this deployment, so local code search can't run here.

ask.title: Ask about this code
ask.body: The answer is generated on your device from the chunks it retrieved, and every part of it is traceable to the file and line it came from.
ask.placeholder: Where is the session token refreshed?
ask.needModel: Install an on-device model to ask questions.
ask.failed: The on-device model couldn't answer that.

answer.title: Answer
answer.empty: The on-device model didn't answer that question.
answer.stoppedEmpty: You stopped this before the model wrote anything.
answer.stoppedKept: This is how far the model got before you stopped it, so it may be cut off mid-sentence. Sources are listed only for a finished answer.

edit.title: Suggest a change
edit.body: Describe the change and name the file. You see the exact diff before anything is written, and writing asks for permission separately.
edit.instructionPlaceholder: Return a 400 instead of throwing when the id is missing.
edit.needIndex: Index the folder and install an on-device model first.
edit.noChange: The model didn't produce a change for that file.
edit.noChangeNeeded: That file already does what you asked — no change needed.
edit.applyHint: This overwrites the file in the folder you opened.
edit.permissionDenied: Write permission wasn't granted, so nothing was changed. Choose Apply again to be asked once more.

privacy.title: Everything here stays on your device
privacy.body: The folder you open is read by this browser tab alone. File contents, the search index and your questions are never sent to VegaDūta or anywhere else, and the reply is generated by the model installed on this machine.
privacy.free: Free — nothing here spends your hosted quota, because nothing here is ever sent to a server to be answered.
privacy.signIn: The console around this page needs a VegaDūta sign-in, but the page itself never reads your account, your plan or your tenant.

studioPage.pageSubtitle: A running gallery of what your AI staff have already created — plus two free, on-device ways to turn it into motion.
studioPage.galleryEmptyBody: Ask any agent to generate an image in the Playground — it shows up here the moment it's ready.
studioPage.clipBodyMotion: Motion+: an agent imagines a short keyframe sequence, and your device fills in the motion between them — agent-directed animation, free and rendered entirely on your device. Prefer something simpler? Still turns any photo into a pan-and-zoom clip in one click. Neither is cinematic AI footage — both are honest, stylised motion.
studioPage.clipBodyStill: Turn a still image into a short pan-and-zoom motion clip, rendered entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded and there is no per-clip charge. A stylised motion clip, not cinematic AI footage.
studioPage.imageBody: Any of your agents can create images — just ask in chat, e.g. "generate an image of a sunrise over Bengaluru". It lands in your gallery above, on your Files page, and ready to animate in Clip Studio.
studioPage.imageAllowanceNote: Platform default limits — your workspace's exact allowance may be tuned by the platform admin.
studioPage.quickHint: Describe it, pick a look, and an agent makes it in the Playground.

templateSetupGuide.subtitle: Picking a template fills in the agent's instructions and nothing else. Here is everything else that has to be in place before it does real work, in the order to do it.
templateSetupGuide.footerHint: Nothing is created until you name the agent and submit the form.
templateSetupGuide.checking: Checking what this workspace already has…
templateSetupGuide.checkFailed: We could not read this workspace's setup, so nothing below is ticked off. The steps themselves are still accurate.
templateSetupGuide.adminOnly: Connecting servers, channels and credentials is restricted to workspace admins. If that is not you, send this list to whoever administers the workspace.
templateSetupGuide.stepKnowledgeTitle: Upload the documents this agent should answer from
templateSetupGuide.stepKnowledgeBodyRequired: This agent's whole job is answering from your material. Until a knowledge collection holds real content, it is no better than a plain chat model.
templateSetupGuide.stepKnowledgeBodyRecommended: This agent is noticeably better when it can quote your own material. Create a knowledge collection and upload what it should answer from.
templateSetupGuide.stepKnowledgeFreeNote: The Free plan includes one knowledge collection.
templateSetupGuide.stepKnowledgeContentNote: An empty collection does not count. The documents have to be uploaded and indexed before the agent can use them.
templateSetupGuide.stepChannelTitle: Connect the channel your people actually write to
templateSetupGuide.stepChannelBody: This agent is meant to answer real customers, patients or staff, not just you in the console. Connect at least one inbound channel.
templateSetupGuide.stepChannelByoNote: WhatsApp, Telegram and Email are all available on the Free plan, but every channel is bring-your-own account — you supply the Meta, Twilio, Telegram or mailbox credentials.
templateSetupGuide.stepGoogleBody: One consent flow unlocks the built-in Gmail, Calendar, Drive and Sheets tools. Without it those tools are present but fail on first use.
templateSetupGuide.stepGoogleNotMcpNote: This is the supported Google path. It is not the same thing as the google-drive MCP server in the tools catalog, which needs a credentials file on the server host instead.
templateSetupGuide.stepE2bTitle: Add an E2B key and turn on code execution for this agent
templateSetupGuide.stepE2bBody: Running code needs a workspace-level E2B credential and a configured code-execution template.
templateSetupGuide.stepE2bBothNote: Both halves are required, and so is the agent's own code-execution toggle. A key on its own leaves the tool listed but dead.
templateSetupGuide.stepCodeIntelBody: Without an index, the code-search tools return nothing and the agent quietly falls back to guessing — the one thing this template promises not to do.
templateSetupGuide.stepCodeIntelUncheckableNote: There is no endpoint that tells this page whether a repository is indexed, so this step is never ticked automatically. Check it yourself on the Code Intel page.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpTitle: Switch on the MCP servers this agent needs
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpBody: A template cannot enable a server for you — there is no per-template or per-agent MCP setting in this product. Enable these on the Tools page and they reach every agent in the workspace.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpBodyNone: None. This agent works with what is already built in, and deliberately so — nothing here should be reaching a browser, a database or the open web.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpCatalogOnlyNote: Only servers from the built-in catalog are suggested. Anything else you add yourself needs a platform review before it can connect.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpFreeCapNote: The Free plan allows two MCP connectors in total, and only ones from the built-in catalog.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpUsage: Connectors registered in this workspace: {used} of {cap}.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpUsageUncapped: Connectors registered in this workspace: {used}. Your plan has no cap.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpCapReached: You are at your plan's connector limit. Turn one off, or upgrade, before adding another — otherwise the request is simply refused.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpExceedsFree: This template needs more connectors than the Free plan allows. It cannot be fully set up without upgrading.
templateSetupGuide.mcpEitherOr: Either one of these — you do not need both.
templateSetupGuide.mcpStateError: On, but the last connection failed
templateSetupGuide.mcpNoCredential: No credentials to find. One click to switch it on.
templateSetupGuide.mcpOAuth: Sign-in happens on Atlassian's own consent screen. There is no key to paste, and a pasted token will not work.
templateSetupGuide.mcpNeedsCredential: You will need: {vars}. Get this from the third-party account first — we cannot issue it.
templateSetupGuide.mcpServerPath: Needs {vars}, which is a file path on the server itself, not a value you can paste from your laptop. Whoever runs the deployment has to set this up.
templateSetupGuide.mcpDeployment: Needs {vars}, and only works if the deployment was set up for this server. Ask whoever runs it before promising anyone this will work.
templateSetupGuide.mcpFindHint: On the Tools page, look for the card named “{name}”.
templateSetupGuide.mcpSecretNote: Store keys in the workspace vault and reference them as {{secret.NAME}} from the server's config, so they resolve inside the tool boundary. Never paste a key into a chat with the agent.
templateSetupGuide.stepAllowListTitle: If you restrict this agent's tools later, include the MCP names
templateSetupGuide.stepAllowListBody: MCP tools reach an agent under a prefixed name. This template does not set a tool allow-list, so anything you switch on above reaches it automatically — no extra step today.
templateSetupGuide.stepAllowListNamesNote: The moment you do restrict this agent's tools, the prefixed MCP names have to be in that list too, or they are silently dropped. The agent's own tool-access screen lists the real names.
templateSetupGuide.stepCreateTitle: Create the agent and brief it
templateSetupGuide.stepCreateBody: Using this template pre-fills the create form on the Agents page. Review the instructions, change what does not match your business, name it and submit.
templateSetupGuide.reasonRepo: Reads the repository this agent is supposed to reason about, instead of whatever it can infer from the conversation.
templateSetupGuide.reasonWebSearch: Lets the agent look things up beyond what it was trained on.
templateSetupGuide.reasonErrors: Pulls the actual stack traces and error groups rather than reasoning about a pasted fragment.
templateSetupGuide.reasonTeamChat: Reads from and posts to your team's Slack.
templateSetupGuide.reasonEscalate: For handing a conversation to a human — escalation only, not day-to-day answering.
templateSetupGuide.reasonDatabase: Read-only queries against a database you point it at.
templateSetupGuide.reasonBrowseSite: Opens a page the way a browser would, for sites with no API.
templateSetupGuide.reasonSmartHome: Controls the devices in your own Home Assistant setup.
templateSetupGuide.cautionSmartHome: This one moves things in your actual home. Read exactly what your Home Assistant exposes before switching it on, and keep the agent supervised.

workflowNodesAi.question_classifierDescription: A model reads the text and picks exactly one of your classes, then the run follows that class's branch. Anything unclear goes to your default class.
workflowNodesAi.parameter_extractorDescription: Pulls named, typed values (text, number, yes/no, list, choice) out of free text. Values the text does not state stay empty, and missing required ones are reported.
workflowNodesAi.variable_aggregatorDescription: Takes the first of several earlier results that actually has a value. No model call.
workflowNodesAi.document_extractorDescription: Turns an uploaded PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, text, Markdown or HTML file (or a web page) into plain text, with size limits.
workflowNodesAi.classifierHint: A model classifies the text at temperature 0. Its reply must name one of your classes exactly; anything else - an error, an unknown class, low confidence - sends the run to the default class. Draw one connection from each class port.
workflowNodesAi.classDescriptionPlaceholder: What belongs in this class, e.g. questions about invoices, refunds or payments
workflowNodesAi.classesHandleHint: The handle names the connection: renaming it disconnects any branch already drawn from that class. Use letters, digits and dashes.
workflowNodesAi.minConfidenceHint: If the model's confidence is below this, the run takes the default class instead. 0 turns the check off.
workflowNodesAi.textHint: Leave blank to use this node's input. Earlier results can be inserted with {{ }} expressions.
workflowNodesAi.instructionPlaceholder: e.g. Treat anything about a chargeback as billing
workflowNodesAi.modelOverrideHint: Only used when you bring your own provider key. Workspaces on the platform model always use the platform's model. Leave blank to use your active provider's default.
workflowNodesAi.extractorHint: A model reads the text and fills these parameters as strict JSON. It is told to answer null for anything the text does not state, and it never fills in a guess. An unusable reply is retried once.
workflowNodesAi.paramDescriptionPlaceholder: What to look for in the text
workflowNodesAi.extractorOutputHint: The output is a JSON object with one key per parameter (null when the text does not state it) plus "_missing", the required parameters that could not be filled. Add a Condition node after this one to branch on _missing.
workflowNodesAi.aggregatorHint: Picks the first source that has a value. Each source is usually an earlier step's output, inserted as an expression.
workflowNodesAi.aggregatorLimitHint: A run follows one path, so this node does not wait for or merge branches. It reads the outputs of earlier steps by their label and picks the first with a value; a step that did not run counts as empty.
workflowNodesAi.documentHint: Reads a file or text and outputs plain text. PDF and Word files go through the same extractor as Knowledge uploads. The result is plain text, never run as anything.
workflowNodesAi.documentSourceHint: An uploaded file's attachment key (chat-attachments/...), a web page URL, or the text itself. Web pages and text files can be read from a URL; PDF, Word and Excel files must be uploaded and passed by their attachment key.
workflowNodesAi.documentOutput_json: JSON with text, type, pages and whether it was cut
workflowNodesAi.limitsHint: Blank uses the workspace limits. A step can lower these limits but never raise them; anything past a limit is cut and the result says so.
workflowNodesAi.problem_emptyHandle: A class has no handle - give every class a short name.
workflowNodesAi.problem_handleTooLong: The handle "{value}..." is too long (64 characters at most).
workflowNodesAi.problem_reservedHandle: "{value}" is reserved for the failure port - choose another handle.

httpNode.httpDescription: Call any public REST API or webhook - method, URL, headers, body - and pass the response on.
httpNode.templateHintInput: is this node's raw input; when it's a JSON object every top-level field is also addressable as
httpNode.templateHintJson: is the input as a JSON string literal, safe to embed inside a JSON body.
httpNode.insertSecret: Insert a vault secret as a header…
httpNode.secretsHintPrefix: Never paste a real key here. Store it in the vault and reference it as
httpNode.secretsHintSuffix: - the value is filled in server-side at run time and redacted from every response, log line and agent transcript.
httpNode.bodyHintJson: Sent with Content-Type: application/json unless you set your own Content-Type header.
httpNode.bodyHintForm: A JSON object of fields is encoded as key=value&… for you; anything else is sent exactly as typed.
httpNode.saveAsHint: Blank: the response body becomes this node's output. A field name: the output is the input's own fields plus that field holding {status, ok, headers, body}, so later nodes can address both by name.
httpNode.failOnHttpErrorLabel: Treat non-2xx responses as failures (the node is skipped and its input passes through)
httpNode.ssrfNote: Only public http(s) hosts are allowed: private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses are refused, and redirects are followed for at most 3 hops. Responses are capped at 20,000 characters.

workflowNodesData.setDescription: Add or change fields on the data. Values can use expressions.
workflowNodesData.filterDescription: Keep only the items of a list that match your conditions.
workflowNodesData.sortDescription: Order a list by one or more fields - numbers, dates or text.
workflowNodesData.aggregateDescription: Count, sum, average or combine a list, optionally grouped by a field.
workflowNodesData.limitDescription: Keep only the first or last N items of a list.
workflowNodesData.dedupeDescription: Drop repeated items, comparing whole items or chosen fields.
workflowNodesData.switchDescription: Send the run down one of several named paths by matching conditions.
workflowNodesData.mergeDescription: Combine inputs: append them, join on a key, or take the first non-empty one.
workflowNodesData.summaryMergeNoKey: Pick a key to join on
workflowNodesData.itemsFieldHint: Leave blank when the previous step's output is the list itself. If the list sits inside an object such as {"rows": [...]}, type its field name - the rest of the object is kept.
workflowNodesData.regexHint: Regex uses Java syntax. A pattern can be at most 200 characters, values longer than 10,000 characters are not tested, and every match has a short time limit.
workflowNodesData.setHint: Each field is written onto the data from the previous step. Values may use expressions such as {{ $json.total }}; they are worked out once for this step (put Set inside a Loop to compute per item).
workflowNodesData.setTypeHint: Auto turns numbers, true/false, null and JSON into real values; pick Text to keep something like 01234 exactly as written.
workflowNodesData.keepOnlySetLabel: Keep only the fields set here (drop everything else)
workflowNodesData.filterHint: Numbers compare as numbers and ISO dates as dates; everything else compares as text. Items without the field never match greater/less comparisons.
workflowNodesData.sortHint: Stable: items that tie keep their order. Missing or empty values always sort last.
workflowNodesData.aggregateHint: Without a group the result is one object; with a group it is a list with one object per group, in order of first appearance.
workflowNodesData.groupByPlaceholder: a field, or several separated by commas
workflowNodesData.limitHint: Keeps the first or last N items of the list. N may be an expression.
workflowNodesData.dedupeHint: Compares the chosen fields (or whole items). Values of different types are different: 1 and "1" are not duplicates.
workflowNodesData.dedupeByPlaceholder: id, email - blank compares whole items
workflowNodesData.switchHint: Cases are tested top to bottom and the first one that matches decides the path. Each case becomes an output port named after it; anything unmatched leaves through Default. Fields are read from the incoming data (a blank field tests the whole text).
workflowNodesData.caseReservedWarn: This name is reserved - pick another.
workflowNodesData.caseDuplicateWarn: Another case already has this name - names must be unique.
workflowNodesData.mergeHint: Combines what reaches this step. After a Parallel, Fan-out or Loop step the input is a list with one entry per branch or item, and that is what gets merged. To combine named steps instead, add sources below. A run follows one path, so Merge cannot wait for branches that never ran - it combines what is present.
workflowNodesData.mergeMode_append: Append - put all inputs in one list
workflowNodesData.mergeMode_join: Join - match rows on a key
workflowNodesData.join_left: All rows of the first input
workflowNodesData.join_inner: Only rows found in every input
workflowNodesData.minInputsHint: If fewer inputs than this are present the step is skipped instead of producing a thin result. 0 means no minimum.

workflowForms.waitDescription: Pause the run for a set time, until a date, or until an outside call resumes it. The pause is stored, so it survives restarts.
workflowForms.formHint: A public page where anyone with the link fills in the fields below. Each submission starts a run whose input is a JSON object keyed by field key. The form uses this trigger's webhook link, so switch the webhook on first.
workflowForms.formEnableWebhookFirst: Switch the webhook on above to get the form link.
workflowForms.formOauthNotSupported: A form needs the secret-token webhook mode, not OAuth2.
workflowForms.formRedirectIssue: The redirect must be an https:// link.
workflowForms.formNoFields: No fields yet - add at least one.
workflowForms.formKeyIssueInvalid: Keys start with a letter and use only letters, digits and _.
workflowForms.waitModeWebhook: Until an outside call resumes it
workflowForms.waitUntilHint: An ISO 8601 date-time (a bare date means midnight UTC). Expressions from earlier nodes are allowed.
workflowForms.waitTimeoutLabel: Give up after (hours, blank = the maximum)
workflowForms.waitCapHint: A wait can last at most the limit set for this deployment (7 days by default). Wake-ups run on a short sweep, so expect the run to continue within about a minute of the time.
workflowForms.waitWebhookHint: The run gets a private resume link. Put {{$run.waitUrl}} in an earlier node (an email, an HTTP call, an agent message) to hand it to whoever should continue the run. Workflow editors can also read it from the run's wait details. POSTing JSON to it continues the run and the JSON becomes this node's output. The link works only while the run is parked at a Wait node.
workflowForms.waitFeatureHint: Wait nodes only run when this deployment has them switched on; otherwise the workflow fails validation instead of skipping the wait.
workflowForms.onError_continue: Continue, passing the error on as this node's output
workflowForms.onError_branch: Follow the red error port if one is connected, otherwise stop
workflowForms.errorStrategyHint: Only applies when this deployment has the node error strategy switched on; otherwise the node behaves exactly as before.
workflowForms.retryEnabledLabel: Retry this node when it fails
workflowForms.retryRiskHint: This node can send or change something outside the workflow, so it is not retried unless you allow it below. A duplicate send is worse than a failure.
workflowForms.retryUnsafeLabel: Retry anyway - I accept a possible duplicate side effect
workflowForms.pageUnavailableBody: The link may be wrong, or its owner has turned the form off.
workflowForms.pageBusy: We're having trouble reaching the form. Please refresh and try again.
workflowForms.pageRateLimited: Too many submissions in a short time. Please wait a minute and try again.
workflowForms.pageTooLarge: That submission is too large. Please shorten it and try again.
workflowForms.pageRedirecting: Taking you to the next page...
workflowForms.error_out_of_range: That number is out of range.
workflowForms.error_invalid_body: Something went wrong with that submission. Please refresh and try again.

openApiTools.readOnlyNote: Only workspace admins can import, refresh, or change API sources. Every agent in the workspace can already call the tools listed here.
openApiTools.emptyBody: Point the platform at an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 document and every operation in it becomes a tool your agents can call - no code to write.
openApiTools.importTitle: Import an API from its OpenAPI document
openApiTools.importIntro: Give the API a name, then paste the document or its URL. You will pick which operations to turn into tools on the next step.
openApiTools.stepReview: Step 2 of 2 · operations, base URL and auth
openApiTools.prefixHelp: Every generated tool is named <prefix>_<operation>, so two APIs with a "listUsers" never collide. Lowercase letters, digits, underscores.
openApiTools.specUrlHelp: Public http(s) URL of a JSON or YAML OpenAPI 3 / Swagger 2 document. URLs inside the platform's own network are refused.
openApiTools.nameRequired: Give the API a name first.
openApiTools.previewFailed: The document could not be read.
openApiTools.operationsFound: {count} operations found · tools will be named {prefix}_…
openApiTools.baseUrlHelp: Every operation's path is appended to this. Pre-filled from the document's first server when it declares one. Must be a public http(s) address.
openApiTools.baseUrlRequired: Enter the base URL the API is served from.
openApiTools.oauth2ClientIdPlaceholder: e.g. the API key from your developer portal app
openApiTools.oauth2ScopePlaceholder: space-separated, if the provider requires it
openApiTools.oauth2Help: The platform fetches a short-lived access token from the token URL, caches it until just before it expires, and sends it as Authorization: Bearer on every call. A 401 retries once with a fresh token.
openApiTools.oauth2Required: OAuth 2.0 needs a token URL, client ID and client secret.
openApiTools.secretPlaceholder: Stored encrypted; never shown again. {{secret.NAME}} references a workspace vault secret.
openApiTools.secretKeepPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the stored credential ({preview})
openApiTools.secretHelp: Encrypted at rest with the platform key and only decrypted for the duration of a call. Use {{secret.NAME}} to reference a workspace secret from the vault instead of pasting a value.
openApiTools.secretRequired: Enter the credential for the selected authentication.
openApiTools.selectAtLeastOne: Select at least one operation to import.
openApiTools.importedToast: "{name}" imported - {count} tools are live for your agents.
openApiTools.refreshTitle: Re-read the document and update the tools
openApiTools.loadToolsError: Could not load the tools of this API.
openApiTools.tryItHelp: The JSON an agent would send as the tool input. Runs the real request against the API with the stored credential and shows exactly what the agent would receive.
openApiTools.nameAndBaseUrlRequired: Name and base URL are both required.
openApiTools.prefixImmutableNote: The tool prefix ({prefix}) cannot change - agents may already rely on the generated tool names. To re-read the document itself, use Refresh.
openApiTools.deleteDialogBody: Its {count} generated tools disappear from every agent immediately and the stored credential is erased. This cannot be undone.

toolPolicies.title: Tool argument policies
toolPolicies.intro: Limit what this agent may pass to a tool. A call that breaks a rule is refused before the tool runs, and the agent is told why. Rules can only tighten what the agent may do, never grant more.
toolPolicies.none: No argument policies on this agent.
toolPolicies.denyUnlisted: any argument not listed is refused
toolPolicies.editorHelp: One entry per tool, or per name pattern such as mcp__files__*. Each rule names an argument path (url, opts.limit, items[*].id) and checks: type, enum, minLength, maxLength, min, max, pattern, urlHostIn, pathUnder, maxItems, required, forbidden.
toolPolicies.errorShape: The document must be an object with a policies list.
toolPolicies.errorEmpty: Enter a policy document, or use Remove all.
toolPolicies.errorTooLarge: The document is larger than {max} characters.
toolPolicies.errorTooManyPolicies: At most {max} tools can have a policy.
toolPolicies.errorPolicyShape: Policy {n} needs a tool name and a list of rules.
toolPolicies.refusalNote: A refused call appears in this agent's activity as the tool's result and in the audit log as tool.arg_policy.denied. Argument values are never written to the log.

trajectoryEval.intro: The tool calls this agent should make for this case, in order. One step per line: a tool name, optionally followed by a JSON object of argument matchers.
trajectoryEval.loadFailed: Could not load the expected trajectory.
trajectoryEval.otherGrader: This case already has a response grader (regex, exact or JSON schema). A case holds one grader, so clear that one before adding an expected trajectory.
trajectoryEval.toollessHint: This dataset replays without tools, so the trajectory is saved but cannot be scored. Turn on tool execution for the dataset to score it.
trajectoryEval.modeExact: Exact: same calls, same order, nothing extra
trajectoryEval.modeInOrder: In order: extra calls allowed in between
trajectoryEval.stepsHelp: An argument matcher is a literal value, {"regex":"..."}, {"present":true} or {"absent":true}. Leave the list empty to expect no tool calls.
trajectoryEval.saved: Expected trajectory saved. Run the dataset again to score it.
trajectoryEval.saveFailed: Could not save the expected trajectory.
trajectoryEval.errorMinScore: Pass at score must be a number from 0 to 1.
trajectoryEval.errorMaxExtra: Max extra calls must be a whole number from 0 to 1000.
trajectoryEval.errorMinEfficiency: Min efficiency must be a number from 0 to 1.
trajectoryEval.errorToolName: Line {line}: start with a tool name (letters, digits and _ - . : only).
trajectoryEval.errorArgsJson: Line {line}: the argument matchers are not valid JSON.
trajectoryEval.errorArgsObject: Line {line}: the argument matchers must be a JSON object.
trajectoryEval.errorArgKey: Line {line}: argument names are field names joined by dots, like opts.limit.
trajectoryEval.errorTooManyArgs: Line {line}: too many argument matchers on one step.
trajectoryEval.noActual: The agent made no tool calls.
trajectoryEval.truncated: Only the first {max} actual calls are compared.

trajectoryEval.useActualConfirm: Replace this case's expected trajectory with the tool names this run called?

judgeCalibration.title: Judge calibration
judgeCalibration.description: Check that the LLM which grades your evals agrees with human reviewers. Kappa is agreement beyond chance (1 is perfect, 0 is no better than guessing); order-swap consistency shows whether the judge changes its mind when the two answers swap places.
judgeCalibration.loadFailedBody: This is a load failure, not an empty list.
judgeCalibration.createHelp: Paste one comparison per line: input, answer A, answer B, which one a human preferred (A or B), and an optional reason. CSV or a copy from a spreadsheet both work. Quote any field that contains commas or line breaks. At least 20 rows are needed to run a set; 30 or more are recommended.
judgeCalibration.namePlaceholder: Set name, for example Support tone v1
judgeCalibration.rowsPlaceholder:
input,answer A,answer B,human label,reason
How do I reset my password?,Click Forgot password on the sign-in page.,Contact your administrator.,A,A is direct and complete

judgeCalibration.deleteBody: This removes the set, its rows and its calibration history. Eval runs are not affected. This cannot be undone.
judgeCalibration.historyHelp: Newest first. A falling kappa means the judge has drifted from your reviewers; re-run after changing the judge model.
judgeCalibration.kappaUndefined: Kappa is undefined for this set: the human labels or the judge used only one answer position throughout. Add rows where the preferred answer differs.
judgeCalibration.notRecorded: Not recorded in the history: the judge returned no usable verdicts, so nothing was measured.

judgeCalibration.badgeUncalibratedHint: This judge has never been calibrated against human labels, so its scores are unverified.

explainersAgents.hookIntro: What happens each time this agent wants to use a tool. Hooks run in the order listed, workspace defaults first.
explainersAgents.hookAskTitle: The model asks to use a tool
explainersAgents.hookAskBody: It names the tool and the arguments it wants to pass.
explainersAgents.hookBeforeBody: Only enabled hooks that match this tool take part. A webhook hook can also allow or refuse the call, and a log hook only records it.
explainersAgents.hookAllowBody: no hook objects, so the call goes ahead
explainersAgents.hookRedactBody: matching text is removed from the arguments first; if that cannot be done safely, the call is not run
explainersAgents.hookApprovalBody: the call waits in the approvals queue and does not run until a person approves it
explainersAgents.hookBlockBody: the call is not run, because a hook blocks it or its rate limit is used up, and the agent is told why
explainersAgents.hookRunBody: With the arguments that passed the checks.
explainersAgents.hookAfterBody: They see the result before the model does. A hook can also add a short note after it.
explainersAgents.hookAfterRedactBody: matching text is removed from the result before the model reads it
explainersAgents.hookAfterBlockBody: the model is told the result was withheld, and why
explainersAgents.hookRecordBody: Blocks, approvals, redactions and hook failures are written to the audit log as agent.hook.decision.
explainersAgents.policyIntro: What happens when this agent calls a tool that has a policy here.
explainersAgents.policyAskTitle: The model asks to use a tool
explainersAgents.policyAskBody: It names the tool and the arguments it wants to pass.
explainersAgents.policyCheckTitle: The arguments are checked against the policy
explainersAgents.policyCheckBody: Each rule looks at one argument. This happens before any approval step. A tool with no policy is not checked here.
explainersAgents.policyAllowedBody: every rule passes, so the call moves on to the usual approval and safety checks
explainersAgents.policyDeniedBody: the tool is not run. The agent is told which argument broke which rule, never the value, and can correct it and try again
explainersAgents.policyRecordBody: It appears in the audit log as tool.arg_policy.denied. Argument values are never written to the log.

helpPrimer.title: Agentic AI, in plain terms
helpPrimer.tourBody: New here, or want a refresher? Nine illustrated steps walk you through every part of the console, in about two minutes.
helpPrimer.docsBody: The full reference — getting started, agents, workflows, knowledge, tools & MCP, channels, plans, security, and troubleshooting — with jump-links into every screen.
helpPrimer.recipesBody: Real, buildable automations for advertising, call centers, UPI payments, retail, healthcare and more — mapped to {brand}'s workflow nodes.
helpPrimer.intro: A chatbot answers a question and stops. An agent is different: it plans a path to a goal, uses tools to get real work done, takes multiple steps on its own, works across channels like chat, email, and voice, and asks a human when a decision truly matters. The shorthand: a chatbot talks, an agent does.
helpPrimer.card_plan_body: An agent breaks a goal into steps, decides what to do next, and works across your channels — where a chatbot just replies to the last message.
helpPrimer.card_tools_body: Agents call APIs, search your documents, run code, and update systems — taking multiple steps to finish a job rather than only producing text.
helpPrimer.card_ask_body: Good agents know their limits: they pause for a human to approve high-stakes actions, so you stay in control of what actually happens.
helpPrimer.nowBody: The industry is shifting from AI that talks to AI that does. Instead of a clever autocomplete, you get a teammate that can carry a task from start to finish — drafting, checking, calling systems, and following up. Major analysts, including Gartner and Deloitte, expect enterprises to adopt AI agents rapidly through 2026. The practical upshot for you is simpler: agents multiply what one person can get done.
helpPrimer.worthBody: Directing AI is becoming the next core literacy — the way spreadsheets, the web, and mobile each became baseline skills in their turn. The workforce is being reshaped by the people who learn to direct agents, not replaced by them. Students and professionals who actually build with agents gain a compounding edge: every workflow you hand off well makes the next one easier to hand off too.
helpPrimer.learnBody: The fastest way to understand agents is to build one. On {brand} you can stand up a real, working agent for free in an afternoon, ground it in your own documents so it answers from what you know, and use code intelligence to learn directly from real codebases. From there you add the parts that make an agent trustworthy — guardrails that keep it in bounds and evaluation that measures whether it is actually doing the job well. It is hands-on the whole way: you learn agentic AI by shipping one.

evalControls.saveFailed: Could not save the replay mode.
evalControls.modeHelp: Choose whether a replay may use the agent's tools. This changes what the next run measures.
evalControls.modeTextOnlyHelp: The agent answers without its tools. Safe: nothing real happens. Expected-tool checks cannot be met.
evalControls.modeFullHelp: The same tools, guardrails and step limits a live user gets. Needed for expected-tool and trajectory checks.

evalControls.autoApproveNeedsFull: Switch on the full pipeline first: auto-approval only applies when tools run.
evalControls.autoApproveConfirmBody: Every tool call in this dataset's replays that would wait for a person will be approved automatically. Approved tools that only read run for real; approved tools that could change something are still simulated. Only do this in a workspace with test data. Runs record that they were auto-approved.
evalControls.trajectoryHelpOn: Cases with an expected trajectory are scored on which tools the agent called and in what order. This is switched on for the whole deployment by your administrator, not per dataset.
evalControls.trajectoryHelpOff: Trajectory checks are not available here. They are switched on for the whole deployment by your administrator, and need a plan that includes evals.
evalControls.trajectoryNeedsFull: This dataset is text only, so cases with an expected trajectory will not be scored. Switch on the full pipeline.
evalControls.runAutoApprovedTitle: A person decided none of this run's tool calls; the eval sandbox approved them.

evalControls.modeDefaultHelp: Follows your workspace's setting (the full pipeline unless an admin changed it). Each run can still choose its own mode.
evalControls.datasetModePinnedTitle: This dataset always replays this way. A single run can still choose another mode.
evalControls.datasetModeDefaultTitle: This dataset follows the workspace default for how runs replay.
evalControls.runModeLabel: Replay mode for the next run
evalControls.runModeHelp: Full pipeline runs the agent with its tools, guardrails and approvals in a safe sandbox: tools that only read really run, anything that could change data or send something is simulated. Quick withholds the tools and tests the written answer only.

localModelSettings.title: Speed and behaviour
localModelSettings.reasoningHelp: Models like Qwen 3.5 reason silently before they reply. Off answers in seconds; higher settings think longer and can answer harder questions better, but a laptop may take 30 seconds or more.
localModelSettings.keepHelp: A model that is not loaded takes several seconds to start on the next message. Longer keeps your answers fast and uses memory while it waits.

localModelSettings.contextHelp: How much of the conversation the model can see at once. A bigger window keeps long chats and tool results intact and uses more memory.
